what: v5f design panel: three designs, two judges (synthesis is DESIGN_protocol_v5f_DRAFT_2026_09_25.md)

designs.name: v5f "claim-and-reconcile": crash-consistent mint-and-anchor (no locks, monotone state with atomic claims, a robust mutex with stealing, reconciliation at the next entry, sys.monitoring on 3.12+)
designs.thesis: Every transition of the v5f machinery is a sequence of single GIL-atomic commits: ownership is claimed with dict.setdefault, per-thread bookkeeping is kept as idempotent sets, and marks are only ever added. The steps are ordered so that any prefix leaves a consistent state. The only cross-thread exclusion is a robust mutex: an owner whose frame is no longer on its thread's stack counts as dead, and the next caller steals it. So no exception at any bytecode can leave a lock held, a counter leaked or a mint poisoned, and the next enter or exit reconciles whatever a dead party left. A Python-level profile hook turns every C call into a point where an asynchronous exception can skip the call; measured, about 7% of SIGALRM timeouts inside a section leak the harness's own `with lock:` under setprofile on 3.11-3.13. So v5f observes minted code through sys.monitoring local events on 3.12/3.13 (0 leaks, no cost outside targets), keeps setprofile on 3.11 with the timer-signal precondition refused, and refuses 3.10.

per_finding.how: Provenance now binds the CODE, not only the function object. A link of the declared object or of its own-dict __wrapped__ chain satisfies provenance iff both hold: (1) link.__globals__ is mod.__dict__; (2) link.__code__.co_filename, after realpath and normcase, equals mod.__file__ (a .pyc __file__ is compared without its trailing 'c'), or co_filename starts with '<' (exec-generated code in the module's own globals, e.g. dataclass __init__). A module with no str __file__ refuses FOREIGN_DEFINITION (fail closed, disclosed). The walk is bounded at 16 hops, cycle-detected and reads only C descriptors. Prototype p_prov.py on 3.11-3.13: the round-4 shape B (real.__code__ = stub.__code__) and shape C (FunctionType(stub.__code__, vars(mod))) both refuse. Plain functions, dataclass __init__, foreign wraps chains and the P1 .txt SourceFileLoader shape are admitted. New exam cases: X26b (shape B, before the trace) and X26c (shape C), both FOREIGN_DEFINITION. L-STUB is rewritten to say provenance proves which globals and which source file the code was compiled from. It adds residual R05b: a stub with a forged co_filename, or '<'-compiled code exec'd into the module's globals, passes (deliberate only). The J1-X1 closure row is corrected.

The machinery contains no threading lock at all. Enter and exit exclude each other through a robust mutex: a succession chain of transaction tokens (tid, id(frame), code, succ-dict). Acquire is `last.succ.setdefault('next', me) is me`, one C op. A token is live only if its frame is on sys._current_frames()[tid]'s f_back chain AND that frame's local `me` IS the token. A dead owner's slot is claimed by the next acquirer. A live owner on the same thread refuses REENTRANT, and a live foreign owner held for more than 10 s refuses MACHINERY_BUSY. A skipped release (a profiled C call, a signal, a hook raising) therefore never blocks anyone. _open and _close take no mutex at all. On 3.12/3.13 the monitoring adapter never runs at a C call. Prototype, on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13: an exception injected at every machinery bytecode caused 0 hangs; the SIGALRM sweep, nested inside an outer tracer with a worker-thread probe every 50 cycles, ran 117k-233k cycles with 26k-50k timeouts, 0 mutex holds left and 0 worker hangs. The v5e-style `with RLock` variant (M1) hangs the sweep. The same mechanism in USER code, where a hook raising at a c_call skips the user's own lock release, is a separate disclosure (L-SIGNAL-311).

For a C lru_cache/cache wrapper, F_T is the wrapper's real callee: the unique FunctionType among gc.get_referents(wrapper), which is the C `func` slot, verified identical on 3.10-3.13 by p_cache_callee.py. Resolution refuses NOT_A_FUNCTION ('__wrapped__ was restamped: it is not the function the wrapper calls') unless that callee IS the wrapper's own-dict __wrapped__. The bound-body refusal and the provenance walk both use the real callee. New exam cases: X24b (the wraps-over-lru_cache restamp from the repro) and X24c (the module-level reference variant, whose message must no longer name the wrong function), both NOT_A_FUNCTION. Spec step 4, L-CACHE and the 'nothing is unwrapped' sentence are corrected.

A generator, coroutine or async-generator target is credited per resumption that ran body bytecode. On 3.12/3.13 the monitoring adapter credits only PY_START and PY_RESUME. throw() and close() fire only PY_THROW, never credited: p_mon_gen.py shows 0 starts for dropped, closed or thrown unstarted generators and for close at a bare yield. On 3.11 the setprofile adapter stores frame.f_lasti at the frame's 'call' event in a per-thread pend dict (single writer, cleared at the thread's last close). It credits at the paired 'return' only if f_lasti moved. p_gen_progress.py on 3.10-3.13 confirms: dropped, closed or thrown unstarted generators and coroutines, and close at a bare yield, are never credited; consuming a 2-yield generator counts 3; asyncio.run counts. 3.10 is refused anyway. New exam case X119 pins these shapes to NOT_EXERCISED on every supported version. Versions and Stated limits now describe resumption counts: they are lower bounds, and a throw-resumption with a handler is counted on 3.11 only.

The dispatch cut becomes a monotone identity set _CUT (id(code) -> code). It holds every asyncio.events.Handle._run code object ever seen: captured at styxx.protocol import and again at each __enter__ BEFORE resolution, from vars(asyncio.events.Handle)['_run'], which must be a FunctionType or __enter__ refuses CUT_UNAVAILABLE. The set is never replaced or cleared, so _STOP and its reset at _ACTIVE == 0 are gone. asyncio.events:Handle._run, or any target whose code is in _CUT, refuses the new code RESERVED_TARGET at resolution, so the cut is never minted. A new exit tripwire CUT_MOVED (recorded) fires if vars(Handle)['_run'] is not a function whose code is in _CUT. The hook and the NESTED walk test `_CUT.get(id(f.f_code)) is f.f_code`. Exam cases: X34 (declaring Handle._run gives RESERVED_TARGET), X65b (the stop-cleared composite) and V44 (a `_run`-named helper). Spec lines 155 and 201 are corrected.

__enter__ refuses UNSUPPORTED_VERSION when sys.version_info < (3, 11). It is raised after the entry claim and before anything global is touched, so the tracer is dead and record() gives TRACE_INCOMPLETE. The reason: on 3.10, call_trampoline's FastToLocals/LocalsToFast around every Python profile callback reverts closure writes and keeps deleted locals alive, and no Python-level hook avoids it. My prototype also found a second 3.10-only hazard: importlib.import_module takes a module lock even for loaded modules on 3.10, and under SIGALRM with the hook installed its release is skipped, hanging worker threads (8/8 probes hung). Versions and Scope now read 3.11-3.13, the '3.9 expected like 3.10' line is deleted, and the 'R3 nit: f_locals cost' closure is marked 3.11+ only. Disclosed as over-blocking.

The rule is kept, because it fails closed. 'Sections are calls' and over-blocking #1/#4 now say that under asyncio.eager_task_factory (3.12+), a child task created on the stack of an open opening runs its first synchronous step on that stack. A section opened in that step is same-stack nesting and refuses NESTED_SECTION for the whole trace. The remedy is `await asyncio.sleep(0)` before cov.run_async, or no eager factory. New version-keyed exam cases (>=3.12): X83 expects NESTED_SECTION, and V35 shows the sleep(0) remedy scoring PASS with exact counts. Task-aware NESTED was rejected: it would add an asyncio.current_task dependency to _open and a rule change nobody needs for soundness.

This fails closed. When the refcount gate fires and gc.get_referrers finds no FunctionType holder while gc.get_freeze_count() > 0, exit counts the references to M_T held by VISIBLE referrers other than the mint and F_T. It records CLONE_ALIVE ('gc is frozen: N references are unscannable') if refcount - expected - visible > 0. Prototype t_freeze.py on 3.11-3.13: a clone frozen after creation refuses CLONE_ALIVE, a benign gc.freeze() inside a section passes, and a live generator of T frozen inside the section refuses. That last shape is the disclosed over-block. New exam cases: X57b (freeze with a live clone gives CLONE_ALIVE) and V36 (freeze with no clone gives PASS). The tripwire bullet and L-CLONE text are amended.

The FOREIGN_DEFINITION message follows the own-dict __wrapped__ chain (the same bounded, cycle-detected, descriptor-only walk) to its innermost FunctionType or real cache callee. It names `dict.get(inner.__globals__, '__name__') + ':' + inner.__qualname__` as 'declare this instead', and keeps the file path as a fallback. No user code runs, because __globals__ is read with dict.get and __qualname__ is a C member. Exam X29b checks that the message contains the defining module:qualname. The closure row is corrected.

Over-blocking #14 is rewritten. Code a trace or profile callback runs directly is never credited. Code it runs through sys.call_tracing (pdb's `debug` command) runs with events re-enabled and is credited to the section whose stack it lands on, like L-RUNTIME. That is observed on 3.12/3.13, and on all versions when the callback installs a nested tracer. It does not happen on 3.11, where call_tracing does not re-enable profiling. The shape joins the L-RUNTIME list and is pinned as version-keyed residual R12, which must be re-measured under the monitoring adapter before the freeze. A code fix is not possible: a callback frame cannot be told apart in general.

A finiteness helper `_finite(v)` returns False for an exact int too large for a double. It catches OverflowError only, never Exception, so asynchronous exceptions still propagate. check_metrics reports usable False with the note 'int too large for a float'. score() raises GateSpecError('gate G: metric ... is too large for a float') instead of OverflowError. The smoke flag is read as dict.get(result, 'smoke') and counts as truthy only for exact bool, int, float or str, so a user __bool__ never runs. Exam cases: X117b (a 400-digit int gives REPORTED from check_metrics and a GateSpecError from score) and X117c (a smoke object whose __bool__ raises gives REPORTED).

Aliases are accepted only when the declared OBJECTS are identical. Two declared names that resolve to one F_T through different declared objects refuse NOT_A_FUNCTION ('two different cache wrappers of one body are declared; declare the body'). The bound-body check also refuses when vars(mod) or the holder namespace contains another _CACHE_WRAPPER whose real callee is the body. The remaining case, a sibling wrapper held elsewhere, is disclosed in L-CACHE as 'every execution of the body counts, whatever route reaches it', pinned as residual R13 (sibling called, other declared: PASS). The 'no two distinct callables map to one code object' sentence gets the L-CACHE exception. Exam cases: X24d (both wrappers declared) and X24e (sibling in the same module), both NOT_A_FUNCTION.

There is no global _ACTIVE counter any more: the hook's self-removal uses the thread's opening set, and the cut is monotone. The exit claim `marks.setdefault('exiting', token)` is __exit__'s first statement. A tracer whose exit never began, because an exception landed at __exit__'s RESUME or at its 'call' event, is a zombie: record() refuses TRACE_ACTIVE, it can still run sections, and its mints stay installed (equal code). It is pruned at the next mutex acquisition once its facade is unreachable, which is detected by a callback-free weakref.ref(facade). The first prototype used weakref.finalize, and the SIGALRM sweep interrupted it before it could run ('Exception ignored in finalize'). Frames retained by the registries never reference the facade: marks hold frame-free tokens, and anchors are frames of module-level functions that take the core. The residual 'facade kept alive' is disclosed as L-ZOMBIE, and spec lines 262 and 504 are corrected.

The module registers os.register_at_fork(after_in_child=_forget_in_child). The handler sets _PID, retires every mint (restoring the original if installed and clearing its local monitoring events), clears _BY_FN, _MINTED, _ANCHORS and _TH, resets the mutex chain, and removes the hook if it is ours (3.11). The monitoring tool id is kept, being monotone. Every core records its pid. In another pid, _open returns None, so run() and run_async() just call fn: no section, no credit, no refusal. The robust mutex also heals by itself in a child, because an owner thread absent there counts as dead. Prototype t_lifecycle.py on 3.11-3.13: fork ProcessPoolExecutor jobs that call COV.run('B', g) return normally with no hook, no anchors and original code, and the parent trace has no problems. Over-block #15 is reworded, and the 'bootstrap frame' sentence and the R2-B3 closure are limited to threads. Exam case V47 (fork pool inside a section: parent PASS, children pass through).

Crediting frames that run T's ORIGINAL code would reopen R1-B1 and X48, because factory siblings and pre-trace clones share that code. Over-blocking #12 therefore gains: 'a generator, coroutine or async-generator OBJECT of T created before the trace (or in an earlier trace) keeps T's original code, so its frames are never credited, even when resumed inside a section; create it inside the trace (its callees are still credited)'. L-WHERE's generator example is narrowed to objects created during the trace. The NOT_EXERCISED fixed sentence gains 'generator and coroutine objects created before the trace are never credited'. Pinned as residual R14 (NOT_EXERCISED).

_check_coverage accepts any result for which issubclass(type(result), dict) holds, and still reads it with dict.get, so no subclass get or __missing__ runs. The NO_TRACE message is split into 'no coverage_trace key' and 'coverage_trace is a <type>, not an exact dict (e.g. loaded with object_pairs_hook)'. check_metrics' `present` uses the same test. Exam cases: X93c (a defaultdict result carrying the exact-dict record gives PASS) and X93d (an OrderedDict-loaded trace gives NO_TRACE with the second wording).

On the 3.11 adapter, both the hook's self-removal and the close and exit removals run only `if sys.getprofile() is _hook`, so a profiler that forwards events to our hook is never removed. The PROFILER_LOST note now reads 'the hook was not installed at close; calls after that may not have been observed'. On 3.12/3.13 there is no profile hook, so the finding is moot. Prototype t_func.py (4 versions): a chaining profiler started in a section stays installed and the forwarded target call is counted. New exam case V37 (3.11 keyed) checks it; it is 3.12+ trivially.

The provenance walk steps through the own-dict __wrapped__ of ANY link. The own dict is read through the GetSetDescriptor found in type(link)'s MRO, so no user code runs; a user-defined __dict__ stops the walk. The walk stays bounded at 16 hops and cycle-detected. Only a FunctionType link that passes the globals+file rule can satisfy provenance, and the minted object is still the one bound at the name, so there is no new over-credit route beyond L-STUB/R06. Prototype p_prov.py: `@logged @Memo def fit` is admitted on 3.11-3.13. New exam case V38 (wraps over class-based wrapper: {fit:1}) and a mutation row.

_open normalises a section whose type is a str subclass with str.__str__(section), the C slot, giving an exact str and never 'Sec.G'. A non-str section refuses UNDECLARED_SECTION without being compared, so no user __eq__ runs. Every section key in the record is therefore an exact str. Exam cases: V39 (StrEnum, numpy.str_-like and (str, Enum) sections give PASS) and X78f (an int section gives UNDECLARED_SECTION).

_check_trace_shape tests `type(o['end']) is not str or o['end'] not in _ENDS`, type check first, so membership is never evaluated for an unhashable value. Exam case X103b: end as a list or a dict gives BAD_TRACE from score, and REPORTED from check_metrics without raising.

Every enter and exit transaction starts with _reconcile() under the mutex. It prunes holders that are not live: facade collected, marked 'exited', another pid, a dead entering token with no 'active' mark, or a dead exiting token. Every mint left with no live holder is retired idempotently: restore only if fn.__code__ is m.code, then pop both registries, each step checked by identity. The entry-time CODE_SWAPPED check therefore sees only mints that live tracers hold. Prototype crash sweep invariants C3 (a fresh trace on another thread gives the baseline verdicts) and C5/C7 (registries hold only live holders, and everything is empty once facades are dropped) hold at every injection point on 3.10-3.13. New exam case X92b: a fault between restore and unregister, then a later trace of the same target must PASS.

check_metrics reports 'smoke run' only when the trace is ABSENT, mirroring the v3 rule. Otherwise the note is 'smoke run (score(smoke=True) does not read coverage): ' + str(e). Exam case X117d: a smoke result whose trace refuses NOT_EXERCISED must carry a note containing [V5:NOT_EXERCISED].

Own-dict reads on class, module and instance steps, on the provenance walk and on cache wrappers use C descriptors that cannot raise for valid objects: ModuleType.__dict__['__dict__'], type.__dict__['__dict__'/'__mro__'] and the instance GetSetDescriptor. They have no try, so an asynchronous exception propagates. The only `except Exception` sites left are the import of the declared module and the module's PEP 562 __getattr__, where arbitrary user code runs. There an asynchronous Exception subclass becomes a chained UNRESOLVED refusal, which is disclosed in L-ASYNC-EXC. The harness remedy is to import declared modules before the trace.

The per-thread registry is _TH[tid] = _ThreadRec(openings: set, epoch, pend). There are no counters: membership changes by idempotent set add and discard. An opening is finalised by ONE claim, `o.fin.setdefault('fin', (end, notes))`, followed by unconditional idempotent cleanups: pop the anchor keyed by the frame object, discard from the thread set, remove the hook on the opener thread when its set is empty (3.11), and clear o.frame. Exit detaches all of its openings on every thread whatever their state, and reconciliation does the same for pruned tracers. _open appends to core.openings, then adds to the thread set, then installs the hook, and registers the anchor LAST. The prototype crash sweep, which includes a coroutine section abandoned on a helper thread, leaves thread_openings = 0 and no hook on 3.10-3.13. The counter-style variant M8 is detected. L-ASYNC-EXC now states the envelope: end may read 'open' or 'raised', and notes may gain OPEN_AT_EXIT or PROFILER_LOST.

The cut and Handle._run are validated before resolution. asyncio is imported at module load; imports inside a transition are forbidden. The prototype showed that an interrupted `import asyncio.events` inside __enter__ leaves importlib's module lock held on 3.11. The entry claim makes a tracer single-use, so a retry refuses REENTRY. Inside the transaction a mint is registered with the core as holder BEFORE fn.__code__ is assigned, and local monitoring events are set before install. A failed or abandoned enter leaves a dead entering token, and the next reconciliation prunes it and retires its mints. Prototype t_lifecycle.py on 3.11-3.13: a MagicMock Handle._run refuses CUT_UNAVAILABLE with nothing minted. An audit hook refusing g's __code__ write mid-mint makes enter raise; a retry gives REENTRY and record() gives TRACE_INCOMPLETE; a later trace passes, registries are empty and every code object is restored. The spec gains 'Interrupted enter' next to 'Interrupted exit'.

The PEP 562 branch calls the module's __getattr__(part) twice. If the two products differ (`is not`), resolution refuses NOT_A_FUNCTION: 'module __getattr__ returns a new object on each access; declare the function it forwards to'. Products are never credited by constant code, which would reopen R3-B1. Over-blocking #8 and #9, the R3 PEP 562 closure row and Resolution step 2 ('called twice') are updated. New exam case X13b (deprecation shim gives NOT_A_FUNCTION).

The first statement of __enter__ is the atomic claim `core.marks.setdefault('entering', token) is token`. Exactly one caller wins; every other caller refuses REENTRY, which is always recorded into problems. The claim happens before the (GIL-releasing) imports and resolution, and no lock is held across them. Prototype t_lifecycle.py: 50/50 barrier-synchronised double entries give exactly one entry and exact counts on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13. New exam case X32d (a concurrent double enter: one entry, REENTRY recorded, counts exact) with its mutant (the claim replaced by a check-then-set).

Resolution branches on the real type, never obj.__class__: issubclass(type(obj), types.ModuleType), issubclass(type(obj), type), and type(obj) in (staticmethod, classmethod). Class internals are read with type.__dict__['__dict__'/'__mro__'/'__qualname__'].__get__(cls), the module dict with ModuleType.__dict__['__dict__'].__get__(mod), and the instance dict through the GetSetDescriptor from type(obj)'s MRO (a user-defined __dict__ gives INSTANCE_PATH). Probe p_resolve_c.py on 3.11-3.13: a strict registry whose __getattribute__ raises KeyError, a metaclass __getattribute__, a property __dict__ and a module subclass all resolve or refuse with no user code run. The docstring and the R1-D2 closure row are corrected. New exam case V40 (strict namespace gives PASS like V08).

New violation cases X07b (`section: ""`) and X07c (`section: "sеction"` with a Cyrillic е), both SECTION_DECL, plus mutation-audit row 'SECTION_DECL non-empty / ASCII clauses | X07b / X07c'. The refusal-deletion gate's region is widened to Experiment.__init__'s v5 block.

New case X57c: nested tracers on f. The inner section calls only a same-globals clone of M_T, kept alive past the inner exit and dropped before the outer exit, and the INNER trace must refuse CLONE_ALIVE. The mechanism already scans every mint the exiting tracer held, not only when the mint is released, and the SM1 catalog carries the 'only the last holder' weakening.
New case X55d: nested tracers on f. FunctionType(f.__code__, {})(1) runs while both hold the mint, and BOTH traces must refuse CLONE_CALLED. The shared _credit path marks every holder.

New case X59c: nested tracers. The inner section calls f, then swaps f.__code__ and leaves the swap in place through the inner exit, restoring it before the outer exit. The INNER trace must refuse CODE_SWAPPED; _exit_txn evaluates CODE_SWAPPED for every mint the exiting core holds.

The rule it guarded is replaced by a monotone cut captured before resolution, and Handle._run can no longer be minted. X34 (declaring asyncio.events:Handle._run gives RESERVED_TARGET) pins the refusal. The per-case leftover check gains the invariant `_CUT.get(id(H)) is H` for H = Handle._run.__code__ during and after every case, and the SM1 catalog carries 'cut read after a mint' and 'cut replaced instead of extended'.

New violation case X120: gate A declares f, gate B declares g; cov.run('A', g) then cov.run('B', f). A must refuse NOT_EXERCISED. New valid case V41: gates A and B both declare f and each section calls f once, so each union is exactly {f:1}, never {f:2}.

New valid cases V42 (G_fast[f] and G_slow[g] share section 'run'; one cov.run('run') calls both; PASS with exact unions) and V43 (a gate whose section is 'harness', not its name). New violation case X121 (X[f] with section 'Y', Y[g] with section 'X', the harness opening by gate name) must refuse NOT_EXERCISED. X78g opens a gate NAME that is not a declared section and must refuse UNDECLARED_SECTION; this kills the open-side sibling mutant.

New valid case V44: cov.run('G', _run, 1) with `def _run(cfg): return f() + cfg` in the fixture must score PASS {f:1}, which pins identity, not name, for the cut. The SM1 catalog carries 'cut by co_name'.

New valid case V11c: the declared target sits exactly 16 hops down a foreign functools.wraps chain and must score PASS. Paired with X30b (17 hops gives FOREIGN_DEFINITION), it pins the bound exactly and kills both range(3) and the off-by-one range(16).

New valid case V45: methods of an abc.ABC subclass and of an Enum give PASS {target:1}. New violation case X14b: an inherited method of an ABC subclass gives INHERITED. The mechanism uses issubclass(type(obj), type).

New valid case V10b: the fixture sets sys.modules[__name__].__class__ to a ModuleType subclass and serves the target only through PEP 562 __getattr__, and must score PASS. X16b: a submodule of that class reached after the colon still refuses INSTANCE_PATH.
New violation case X14c: Leaf(Mid(Base)).fit and Model(LoggingMixin, Base).fit must refuse INHERITED (not UNRESOLVED), with the message 'declare the defining class'.

New violation cases X25c (Scorer.fast = staticmethod(lru_cache(None)(_impl)) with _impl bound at module level) and X25d (a wrapper served only through PEP 562, holder None, whose body is module-level). Both must refuse NOT_A_FUNCTION at entry.

New cases X122 (a declaring gate whose bar fails, m=0.0, and whose harness never calls one declared target must refuse NOT_EXERCISED, never return the table's FAIL row) and X122b (the same with a swallowed NESTED_SECTION must refuse NESTED_SECTION). The exam's _res() helper gains a failing-bar variant.

New case X96c: a genuine trace with gates_sha256 popped must refuse BAD_TRACE, never KeyError or STALE_TRACE. New case X78e: a harness that swallows cov.run('G_typo', f) and never opens G's section must refuse UNDECLARED_SECTION, not SECTION_ABSENT. The SM gate's O14 step-order operator targets every adjacent pair of score steps.

X72b asserts that the NOT_EXERCISED message contains the exact substring "dispatched {'<fx>:f': 2}, unattributed {}" on X72's trace, with each count under its own label. It also asserts check_metrics on that result gives G:exercises usable False and a note starting with [V5:NOT_EXERCISED]; X117d covers the smoke variant. The SM2 differential probe flags any future unasserted observable text difference as an EXAM_HOLE.

No clearing exists any more, because the cut is monotone. New case X65b: V15's inner tracer is entered and exited inside the outer; then section A of the outer runs an event loop serving another thread's run_coroutine_threadsafe and call_soon_threadsafe jobs. A must refuse NOT_EXERCISED with dispatched {f:2}.

New valid case V15b: an outer and an inner prereg both name their gate and section 'G', nested on one stack; both must score PASS {f:1}. A second variant uses a case section whose name equals the exam's self-trace section name.

X59d: after the trace exits and before the case's own finally restores the code, assert f59.__code__ is u59.__code__ (the swap is left in place) and f59() returns -59. _retire restores only `if fn.__code__ is m.code`.

X80c, keyed to 3.11: on a case-owned sub-thread, cov.run('G', body) where body calls f and then sys.setprofile(prof). After run returns, sys.getprofile() must be prof and the opening must carry PROFILER_LOST. On 3.12+ the expected outcome is prof installed with no note, because the monitoring adapter never touches profilers.

X80d: a case-owned sub-thread with no other openings runs an entire `with coverage_trace(exp)` and installs a pure-Python profiler inside the with, after its sections. After exit, sys.getprofile() on that thread must be that profiler. In v5f the exit removes the hook only if the exiting thread's set is empty and the hook is ours, so this is testable inside the self-trace, unlike v5e's _ACTIVE==0 block.

X32c: an explicit cov.__exit__() on success plus another in a finally, and __exit__ in a finally after __enter__ raised UNRESOLVED. That trace must score PASS {f:1}, a later independent trace must pass, and the leftovers must be clean. The exit claim `marks.setdefault('exiting', tok)` makes every second exit a no-op by construction, and the SM1 catalog carries 'claim replaced by an unconditional store'.

V28b, keyed to 3.11: coroutine section B opens on a worker thread and suspends; inside section A on the main thread the harness resumes B to completion (a THREAD_HOP close) and then calls A's target. Expected: A {f:1} with no PROFILER_LOST, B with a THREAD_HOP note. _detach removes a hook only when closer tid == opener tid.

X80e, keyed to 3.11: two run_async sections gathered on one loop; task a installs a pure-Python profiler before B opens. B must raise FOREIGN_PROFILER, recorded. On 3.12+ the expected outcome is PASS, since profilers coexist.
X109b: an old trace scored against a gates block that also adds a declared target (both gates_sha256 and the target set differ) must refuse STALE_TRACE.

X75b, keyed to 3.11: inside section G, call f, then sys.setprofile(p) with a pure-Python p, then call g; remove p after the close. G's notes must contain PROFILER_LOST and the NOT_EXERCISED message for g must name it.
X103c: a genuine one-opening trace with end replaced by class S(str) instance S('returned') must refuse BAD_TRACE. X103b covers the unhashable variants.
X112b: a trace carrying a genuine recorded problem (a swallowed UNDECLARED_SECTION) with one calls count set to 0 must refuse BAD_COUNT, not the problem's code.

V46: two threads, alive at once, each open a section and each dispatch g once through their own event loop's call_soon. record()['uncredited']['dispatched'] must equal {g: 2}, and the NOT_EXERCISED message for a gate declaring g must print 2.

The NESTED_SECTION reason now reads 'a call there would be on the stack of two openings of this trace' when o.section == section, and 'one call would count for both sections' otherwise. LAZY_RESULT is only emitted for exact generator, coroutine or async-generator result types (no isinstance, so no user __class__ runs). It now reads 'fn returned a <type>; whatever of its body runs after the section closed does not count', with ' (its body had not started)' appended when the object is in the created state. Mechanism comment line 213 is fixed. X76b and X74d pin both texts.

designs.mechanism_changes:
This builds on v5e mint-and-anchor. Identity (minting, the f_globals test, the tripwires) and attribution (the anchor walk, the Handle._run cut, exactly one opening per tracer) are unchanged in meaning. What is replaced is the state machine and the event source. Numbered for implementation.

M0. Version and adapter gate (first thing after the entry claim; raised, not recorded).
Refuse UNSUPPORTED_VERSION unless sys.version_info[:2] is one of (3,11), (3,12), (3,13), and unless the build has the GIL (refuse when getattr(sys, '_is_gil_enabled', lambda: True)() is False). The atomicity argument below needs the GIL.
Adapter P (sys.setprofile) runs on 3.11; adapter M (sys.monitoring) runs on 3.12 and 3.13.
Tracer id becomes 'styxx.protocol.coverage_trace/3'. /2 traces refuse WRONG_TRACER.
`import asyncio.events` happens at styxx.protocol import. No import may run inside any transition: the prototype showed an interrupted import leaves an importlib module lock held.

M1. State: every piece of shared state is one of three kinds.
(a) A registry changed only by single GIL-atomic C operations.
(b) An immutable value replaced by one STORE.
(c) A monotone map changed only by setdefault.
The registries:
- _BY_FN: {fn: _Mint}. The key holds fn.
- _MINTED: {id(code): _Mint}. The mint holds the code.
- _ANCHORS: {anchor frame object: _Opening}. Frames hash by identity, and the key holds the frame, so an id is never reused.
- _TH: {tid: _ThreadRec(openings=set(), epoch, pend={})}.
- _CUT: {id(code): code}. Monotone: setdefault only, never cleared.
- _GUARD: {'hint': _Txn}, the head of the robust-mutex chain.
- _TOOL: [id or None]. Monotone on 3.12+.
_Mint(fn, original, code=original.replace(), globals, holders=()). holders is a TUPLE, rebuilt only under the mutex; the event path reads it lock-free.
_Core, one per tracer, is what the registries reference: exp; marks (a monotone dict holding 'entering'->_Txn, 'active'->True, 'exiting'->_Txn, 'exited'->True); by_code {id(code): names} (emptied first at exit); names (kept for record); openings (list); problems (list); clone_called (dict); uncredited {tid: ({}, {})}; facade (a weakref.ref with NO callback); pid.
The user-facing _CoverageTracer is a thin facade holding its core.
Every frame the machinery may retain belongs to a module-level function whose locals hold the core, never the facade: the anchor is _run's frame or _run_async's coroutine frame, and marks and mutex records hold frame-FREE _Txn tokens. The prototype showed that a retained dead frame keeps its whole f_back chain, and so the facade, alive.
_Txn(tid, fid=id(frame), code=frame.f_code, succ={}) is created by `me = _txn()`. It is live iff some frame f on sys._current_frames()[tid]'s f_back chain has id(f) == fid, f.f_code is code, and f.f_locals.get('me') is the token. This is exact, holds no frame, and needs no callback.

M2. Robust mutex (enter and exit only; _open, _close, the event path and record() never take it).
_locked(fn, *args): me = _txn(); _acquire(me); out = fn(*args); _release(me); return out. There is deliberately no try/finally.
_acquire walks from _GUARD['hint'] along succ['next'] to the last token r.
- If r is live and r.tid == me.tid: raise GateSpecError('[V5:REENTRANT] ...').
- If r is live on another thread: sleep 0.2 ms and retry; after 10 s raise '[V5:MACHINERY_BUSY] ...'.
- Otherwise (free or dead): claim with `r.succ.setdefault('next', me) is me`. If the claim won, store the hint; if it lost, re-walk.
_release: me.succ.setdefault('next', _Txn(None, 0, None)) (a free token).
A release skipped for any reason (a profiled C call, a signal, a hook raising) is harmless: the owner's frame dies with the exception and the next acquirer steals.

M3. Reconciliation (the first step of every transaction, under the mutex).
For every mint in _BY_FN ∪ _MINTED: keep = the live holders, where a holder is dead iff any of these holds:
- its facade weakref is dead;
- 'exited' is in marks;
- its pid differs from this process's;
- its 'exiting' token is dead;
- 'active' is absent and its 'entering' token is dead.
For each pruned holder h: set h.by_code = {} and _detach every opening of h with ('open', OPEN_AT_EXIT 'pruned: the trace's own exit did not run'). Then m.holders = keep.
If keep is empty, _retire(m), which is idempotent and consistent at every prefix:
- if fn.__code__ is m.code, restore m.original;
- (3.12+) set_local_events(tool, m.code, 0);
- pop _BY_FN if the value is m;
- pop _MINTED if the value is m.

M4. __enter__ (the facade calls _enter(core)).
E0. me = _txn(). If core.marks.setdefault('entering', me) is not me, append a REENTRY problem and raise REENTRY.
E1. M0 gate.
E2. h = vars(asyncio.events.Handle).get('_run'). If type(h) is not FunctionType, refuse CUT_UNAVAILABLE; otherwise _CUT.setdefault(id(h.__code__), h.__code__).
E3. Resolve every target (M8). A target whose F_T is h or whose code is in _CUT refuses RESERVED_TARGET. Aliases are allowed only when the declared objects are identical.
E4. _locked(_enter_txn, core, resolved), which runs, in order:
- reconcile;
- (3.12+) acquire a tool id (M6);
- for each distinct F_T: if a live mint exists and F_T.__code__ is not m.code, refuse CODE_SWAPPED (nothing joined yet);
- for each F_T: if it has a mint, m.holders = m.holders + (core,). Otherwise create it in this exact order: build m (pure); m.holders = (core,); _MINTED[id(m.code)] = m; _BY_FN[fn] = m; (3.12+) set_local_events(tool, m.code, PY_START|PY_RESUME); fn.__code__ = m.code;
- core.names = {...}; core.by_code = dict(core.names).
E5. core.marks['active'] = True, AFTER the mutex is released. Between release and this commit the entering token is live, so no reconciler prunes the core.
E6. Return.

M5. __exit__ (the facade calls _exit(core); it never raises GateSpecError).
X0. If 'active' is not in marks: _locked(_reconcile) and return. This completes any abandoned enter.
X1. me = _txn(). If core.marks.setdefault('exiting', me) is not me, return: a second exit is a no-op.
X2. core.by_code = {} (credit stops; one store).
X3. For o in list(core.openings): _detach(o, tid, ('open', (OPEN_AT_EXIT,))).
X4. probs = CLONE_CALLED entries from dict(core.clone_called).
X5. _locked(_exit_txn), which runs: reconcile (this core is exiting with a live token, so it is kept); then for every mint m holding core: append CODE_SWAPPED if m.fn.__code__ is not m.code; m.holders = tuple(h for h in m.holders if h is not core); _retire(m) if the tuple is empty. A GateSpecError from _locked (REENTRANT or MACHINERY_BUSY) is appended as a recorded problem and exit continues. The unreleased holdership is pruned later, because the exit token dies.
X6. For each mint the core held: the CLONE_ALIVE refcount gate. expected = 2 + (fn.__code__ is m.code). Scan gc.get_referrers only if the gate fires. Record CLONE_ALIVE if any FunctionType other than fn holds M_T, OR (gc.get_freeze_count() > 0 and refcount - expected - visible_refs_excluding_mint_and_fn > 0). Add the CUT_MOVED tripwire.
X7. core.problems.extend(probs) (one call). (3.11) If this thread's opening set is empty and sys.getprofile() is _hook, set the profile to None.
X8. core.marks['exited'] = True (commit).

M6. Event path.
The shared part, _credit(frame, code, m, tid):
- if frame.f_globals is not m.globals: set h.clone_called[id(code)] for every h in m.holders, and return;
- walk f = frame.f_back until the cut (`_CUT.get(id(f.f_code)) is f.f_code`) or the root, collecting _ANCHORS.get(f);
- for each holder h with id(code) in h.by_code, with `mine` being the found openings whose core is h: exactly one opening gets a single-key increment of o.calls[id(code)]; two or more each get an increment of ambiguous; none gets an increment of h.uncredited[tid][0 if cut else 1];
- names are expanded only in record().
Adapter M (3.12/3.13): tool id 3 or 4, whichever is free or already named 'styxx.protocol'; if neither, refuse MONITOR_BUSY. Once taken, the id is kept for the process lifetime (monotone). Callbacks are registered for PY_START and PY_RESUME only, and events are set LOCALLY on each minted code object. PY_THROW and PY_UNWIND are not used: throw() and close() fire only PY_THROW, so they are never credited. The callback: m = _MINTED.get(id(code)); require m and m.code is code; require the thread's opening set to be non-empty (diagnostics then see the same threads as 3.11); then _credit(sys._getframe(1), ...). No handler and no lock. An exception propagates, and the tool is not dropped. At exit, the new MONITOR_LOST note (never refuses) is added if get_tool(id) is no longer ours or a held mint's local events were cleared.
Adapter P (3.11) is the v5e hook, restructured:
- tr = _TH.get(tid); if tr is None or tr.openings is empty: remove the hook ONLY IF sys.getprofile() is _hook, and return;
- a 'return' event returns at once unless tr.pend is non-empty; events other than 'call' and 'return' return;
- identity check;
- generator, coroutine and async-generator code (co_flags & 0x3A0): at 'call', tr.pend[frame] = f_lasti; at 'return', credit only if the frame was pending and f_lasti moved. Other code is credited at 'call'.

M7. _open(core, section, anchor), lock-free (called from module-level _run(core, section, fn, args, kwargs), whose frame is the anchor, and from _run_async).
- If core.pid != this pid, return None; run then just calls fn (fork pass-through).
- Refusals, recorded when active: TRACE_INACTIVE; section normalisation (a str subclass becomes str.__str__(section); a non-str gives UNDECLARED_SECTION without comparing); UNDECLARED_SECTION; NESTED_SECTION, walking anchor.f_back to the cut and matching o.core is core; (3.11) FOREIGN_PROFILER; (3.11, main thread) SIGNAL_TIMER if signal.getsignal() of SIGALRM, SIGVTALRM or SIGPROF is a Python callable.
- tr = _TH.get(tid), or _TH.setdefault(tid, _ThreadRec()).
- ep = next(_EPOCH) if no profiler is installed, else tr.epoch.
- o = _Opening(...) (pure); core.openings.append(o); tr.openings.add(o); (3.11, no profiler installed) tr.epoch = ep and sys.setprofile(_hook); _ANCHORS[anchor] = o (the commit, last).
_close(o, end):
- compute notes (pure): THREAD_HOP if the closing tid is not o.tid; (3.11) PROFILER_LOST if the hook is not ours or the epoch changed; (3.11, main thread) a recorded SIGNAL_TIMER if a timer handler is present now;
- _detach(o, tid, (end, notes)), which runs: o.fin.setdefault('fin', value) (the claim and commit); _ANCHORS.pop(o.frame, None); tr.openings.discard(o); if the closer is the opener and the set is empty, tr.pend.clear() and (3.11) remove the hook if it is ours; o.frame = None.
- run() sets o.lazy only for an exact result type in {generator, coroutine, async generator}.

M8. Resolution and provenance. No user code runs except the import and a module's PEP 562 __getattr__. Those two keep `except Exception`, giving a chained UNRESOLVED; nothing else has a handler.
- Branch on issubclass(type(obj), ModuleType or type) and on type(obj) in (staticmethod, classmethod).
- Read dicts only through C descriptors (M2 of the per-finding notes).
- PEP 562: call __getattr__ twice; if the two products are not identical, refuse NOT_A_FUNCTION.
- Cache wrappers: F_T is the unique FunctionType in gc.get_referents(wrapper), and it must be the own-dict __wrapped__. Refuse NOT_A_FUNCTION if the body is bound by name, or if another cache wrapper of the same body is in vars(mod) or in the holder.
- Provenance: a FunctionType link with __globals__ is mod.__dict__ AND a co_filename matching mod.__file__ (or '<'-prefixed). The walk passes through any link's own-dict __wrapped__ (descriptor read), up to 16 hops, cycle-detected.
- The FOREIGN_DEFINITION message names the innermost module:qualname.

M9. record() is pure.
It needs 'exited' in marks. Otherwise it refuses TRACE_INCOMPLETE if 'exiting' is present, or if 'entering' is present without 'active'; else it refuses TRACE_ACTIVE.
An opening's end and notes come from o.fin (default ('open', ())), plus LAZY_RESULT. Counts are expanded through core.names. uncredited is summed across threads.
The recorded codes add CUT_MOVED, SIGNAL_TIMER, REENTRANT and MACHINERY_BUSY. The notes add MONITOR_LOST.

M10. at-fork: os.register_at_fork(after_in_child=...): set _PID; _retire every mint; clear _BY_FN, _MINTED, _ANCHORS and _TH; reset _GUARD; (3.11) remove the hook if it is ours.

M11. Scoring.
- _check_coverage accepts a dict subclass as the result (read with dict.get), with the split NO_TRACE message.
- _check_trace_shape tests the exact type before `end in _ENDS`.
- check_metrics: _finite catches OverflowError only; smoke is read with exact-type truthiness; 'smoke run' is used only when the trace is absent.
- score() turns an OverflowError from float() into a GateSpecError.
- All other score steps and their order are unchanged. Each step pair is pinned by the new cases.

M12. Deleted: _LOCK, _ACTIVE, _STOP, the _THREADS counts, and weakref.finalize. Every [V5:CODE] literal still sits at its own emission site (G7), and the refusal-deletion gate is converted to mutate by coded LITERAL (see the gate section).
designs.version_policy:
3.10: REFUSED at __enter__ with UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, before anything global is touched. On 3.10, call_trampoline wraps every Python-level profile callback in FastToLocals and LocalsToFast. That reverts closure writes made by other threads and keeps deleted locals alive (round-4 blocker). No pure-Python hook avoids it, and 3.10 has no sys.monitoring. The prototype also found that importlib.import_module takes a module lock even for loaded modules on 3.10, and under SIGALRM with the hook installed that lock's release is skipped: 8 of 8 worker probes hung. The spec deletes the '3.9 expected like 3.10' line. Disclosed as over-blocking.

3.11: SUPPORTED through adapter P (sys.setprofile), with the same state machine as every other version.
Behaviour specific to 3.11:
- FOREIGN_PROFILER and the PROFILER_LOST note (epochs) exist only here;
- generator credit uses the f_lasti progress rule;
- sys.call_tracing does not credit;
- NEW: SIGNAL_TIMER, a recorded refusal at open and at close on the main thread when a Python handler is installed for SIGALRM, SIGVTALRM or SIGPROF.
Why SIGNAL_TIMER: the hook makes each c_call a delivery point where CPython skips the call. Measured under SIGALRM on a `with lock:` loop inside a section, 3606 of 50385 timeouts leaked the harness's own lock, against 0 untraced (7%; the prototype's SIGNAL_TIMER check was not active in this run).
Ctrl-C is disclosed as the residual L-SIGNAL-311. 3.11 is kept because it is the lab's default interpreter (P1 retro, exam). Refusing it is the named alternative if the panel judges L-SIGNAL-311 a corruption on a par with py310.

3.12 and 3.13: SUPPORTED through adapter M (sys.monitoring). Tool id 3 or 4 is held for the process lifetime. Only PY_START and PY_RESUME are enabled, as LOCAL events on minted code objects. The callback never runs at a C call, so the profiled-C-call hazard class is closed structurally for user code as well as for the machinery. Measured: 0 lock leaks out of 51075 (3.12) and 52456 (3.13) timeouts; the setprofile adapter on the same interpreters leaked 3362 and 3553. It also costs nothing outside targets (x1.0 against x11-17 for setprofile on 1M non-target calls), is 2.5-3x cheaper per hit, and coexists with every sys.setprofile and sys.settrace tool (cProfile, profile, yappi, pyinstrument, pdb), so FOREIGN_PROFILER and PROFILER_LOST do not arise. MONITOR_BUSY refuses when tool ids 3 and 4 are both taken by other tools. throw() and close() fire only PY_THROW and are never credited. sys.call_tracing code is credited (L-RUNTIME, version-keyed).

3.14+ and free-threaded builds: REFUSED (UNSUPPORTED_VERSION) until re-validated. The atomicity argument assumes the GIL.

Why two adapters despite v5e's objection: the objection was the doubled exam matrix. Here one state machine, the reconciliation logic, the attribution walk and the crediting code are shared, and the adapter interface is one function, _credit(frame, code, m, tid). The version-keyed expectations are an enumerated list in the prereg: FOREIGN_PROFILER, PROFILER_LOST, SIGNAL_TIMER, MONITOR_BUSY, the throw-resumption count, call_tracing, eager tasks and cProfile. Every other case must be identical on 3.11-3.13. The aux gate's second implementation and the oracle fuzzer run on all three.
designs.new_limits_and_overblocking:
NEW OVER-BLOCKING, each a refusal of a legitimate harness, disclosed:
(1) 3.10 refuses UNSUPPORTED_VERSION entirely, as do 3.14+ and free-threaded builds.
(2) 3.11 only: SIGNAL_TIMER, recorded at open and at close on the main thread, when a Python handler for SIGALRM, SIGVTALRM or SIGPROF is installed. This covers pytest-timeout's signal method, signal.alarm budgets and the exam's own H2 shape on 3.11. Remedy: thread-based timeouts, or 3.12+.
(3) 3.12+: MONITOR_BUSY when other tools hold sys.monitoring ids 3 and 4. v5f holds its id for the process lifetime.
(4) RESERVED_TARGET: asyncio.events:Handle._run, and any function whose code is a recorded cut code.
(5) CUT_MOVED: a harness or library that rebinds Handle._run during a trace refuses every gate.
(6) CUT_UNAVAILABLE: Handle._run is not a plain function at enter (mocked or C-replaced).
(7) FOREIGN_DEFINITION now also refuses:
- modules without a str __file__ (in-memory modules);
- sourceless or relocated installs whose co_filename differs from __file__ (for example conda prefix relocation);
- targets whose __code__ was swapped before the trace (intended).
(8) NOT_A_FUNCTION now also refuses:
- a cache wrapper whose __wrapped__ is not its real callee;
- a PEP 562 attribute that returns a new object on each access (deprecation shims): declare the target;
- two different cache wrappers of one body declared, or held in the same namespace as the declared one.
(9) CLONE_ALIVE while gc is frozen: a frozen or untracked holder of M_T (a live generator or traceback of T frozen in the section) refuses.
(10) A tracer whose __enter__ raised is single-use: a retry refuses REENTRY. Create a new tracer.
(11) REENTRANT: a finalizer or signal handler that enters or exits a tracer during another enter or exit on the same thread.
(12) MACHINERY_BUSY: another thread holds enter or exit for more than 10 s.
(13) Eager tasks (3.12+): a child that opens its section in its first synchronous step refuses NESTED_SECTION for the whole trace. Remedy: await asyncio.sleep(0) first.
(14) Generator and coroutine targets: throw() and close() resumptions are never credited on 3.12+; on 3.11 they are credited only if the frame's f_lasti moved. Generator and coroutine objects created before the trace are never credited.
(15) Sections opened concurrently with the tracer's exit on another thread refuse TRACE_INACTIVE or record as 'open' with zero calls.

CHANGED OR NEW STATED LIMITS:
- L-SIGNAL-311 (new): on 3.11 only, while a section is open on a thread, an async exception can surface at any C call's c_call event, and CPython skips that call. A `with lock:` release (measured: about 7% of SIGALRM timeouts in a lock-dense loop) or an importlib module-lock release during a first-time import can leak, hanging other threads. SIGNAL_TIMER refuses the timer-signal precondition. Ctrl-C (SIGINT) is the remaining residual. 3.12+ is immune (0 of 51k).
- L-ZOMBIE (new): an exception at __exit__'s entry, or at __enter__'s return on a profiled thread, leaves an active tracer. record() refuses. Its minted (equal) code stays installed until the facade is unreachable and the next enter or exit reconciles. A double fault leaving a stale anchor can keep the facade reachable.
- L-ASYNC-EXC (rewritten as the envelope I6): any fault anywhere in the machinery can only lose counts or make a record read 'open', 'raised', OPEN_AT_EXIT or PROFILER_LOST, or make record() refuse. An async Exception landing in the declared module's import or in its PEP 562 __getattr__ becomes a chained UNRESOLVED.
- L-STUB (widened): provenance proves which globals and which source file the code was compiled from, not that it is the original binding. An in-module stub, a wraps-stamped stub, code with a forged co_filename, and '<'-compiled code exec'd into the module's globals are credited (R05, R06, R05b).
- L-CACHE (widened): every execution of the body counts, whatever route reaches it, including a sibling cache wrapper held outside the scanned namespaces (R13).
- L-WHERE (narrowed): generators and coroutines count only if created during the trace (R14).
- L-RUNTIME (widened): sys.call_tracing code (pdb debug) is credited on 3.12/3.13 and not on 3.11 (R12, version-keyed).
- Counts: resumption counts for generators are lower bounds and version-keyed for throw shapes.
- CPython only; GIL only; greenlet and gevent are untested. The robust mutex's liveness check assumes that a frame executing on a thread is reachable from that thread's current frame, which greenlet stack switching breaks.

REMOVED OVER-BLOCKING on 3.12+: pure-Python profilers, yappi, pyinstrument, profile and cProfile all coexist (FOREIGN_PROFILER no longer applies there). Hook loss through a harness's setprofile(None) or a RecursionError drop (#7) no longer applies. The per-event cost on non-target code (#17) is gone.
designs.risks:
WHAT COULD REOPEN ROUNDS 1-3, and the guard for each:
(1) R3-B3 (an exception swallowed in the hook): the monitoring callback must have no handler, and a callback exception propagates without dropping the tool (verified in p_mon.py). A round-5 red team should check RecursionError and KeyboardInterrupt raised inside PY_RESUME of a coroutine driven by asyncio's C Task.
(2) R1-B3/R2-B2/R3-B2 (class B): the monitoring adapter depends on sys._getframe(1) inside a PY_START/PY_RESUME callback being the target frame, with the true f_back chain. It was verified for plain calls, asyncio Handle._run and threads. Unverified: resumption from C (map(next, gens), itertools, the C Task step, contextvars.Context.run, sys.monitoring during another tool's callback). Attack this first on 3.12/3.13.
(3) R1-B1/R3-B1 (class A): minting is unchanged, but local events are set on M_T, so an in-trace clone of M_T fires them. That matches v5e's L-CLONE. A code.replace() copy of M_T gets no events and is never credited, which is correct.
(4) R1-D2 (resolution crashes and user code): the descriptor-only reads should be attacked with C-extension types, __slots__ plus __dict__ mixes, and module subclasses that override __dict__ as a descriptor.
(5) R2-B3 (the hook persists on a thread): on 3.11 a thread's hook stays only while its opening set is non-empty; a zombie's stale opening can keep an inert hook on a thread (L-ZOMBIE).
(6) R3-D3 (finalizer deadlock): there are no locks. The robust mutex refuses REENTRANT instead of waiting, and the event path takes nothing.

WHAT ROUND 5 SHOULD ATTACK FIRST:
(a) Divergence between the two adapters: run the whole exam and fuzzer on 3.11 against 3.12 and look for any outcome outside the enumerated version-keyed list, for example uncredited diagnostics or generator counts.
(b) The robust mutex. Exactness of liveness: a dead frame's id reused by a new frame of the same code, which the `me` identity rule defends. The cost of sys._current_frames() under contention. Exhausting the 10 s BUSY bound with a legitimately slow owner, since the enter transaction iterates all mints. Greenlet-style stack switching.
(c) The crash-sweep scope. The prototype injected on ONE scenario family on the main thread only; inject on two threads, into run_async and THREAD_HOP closes, and into generator targets. The lab's existing fault_injection_v5.py found 2547 of 10371 v5e points broken, 130 of them HANGs; it must be re-run on v5f through the monitoring injector.
(d) The false-refusal surface of provenance co_filename: symlinked checkouts, zipimport, editable installs, .pth-relocated trees, __file__ relative to cwd.
(e) L-ZOMBIE through module-level `cov` globals, and a double fault that leaves a stale anchor keeping the facade alive.
(f) The SIGNAL_TIMER precondition is incomplete: handlers installed and removed within a section, threading-based libraries that route through signal.pthread_kill.
(g) sys.monitoring interplay: another tool calling free_tool_id, restart_events or set_events on our id (the MONITOR_LOST note under-counts only), tool-id squatting, and bugs in 3.12.x instrumentation. The prototype hit a 3.12.3 settrace opcode bug, so re-validate per patch release.
(h) The noise mask and envelope in SM2 could hide a real regression if a field is nondeterministic in the baseline: the mask must be minimal and reported.
Deliberately not done, and the principal residual: 3.11 keeps the setprofile adapter. If the panel ranks L-SIGNAL-311 with py310, refusing 3.11 makes v5f single-adapter.

designs_all.name: v5f "claim-and-reconcile": crash-consistent mint-and-anchor (no locks, monotone state with atomic claims, a robust mutex with stealing, reconciliation at the next entry, sys.monitoring on 3.12+)
designs_all.thesis: Every transition of the v5f machinery is a sequence of single GIL-atomic commits: ownership is claimed with dict.setdefault, per-thread bookkeeping is kept as idempotent sets, and marks are only ever added. The steps are ordered so that any prefix leaves a consistent state. The only cross-thread exclusion is a robust mutex: an owner whose frame is no longer on its thread's stack counts as dead, and the next caller steals it. So no exception at any bytecode can leave a lock held, a counter leaked or a mint poisoned, and the next enter or exit reconciles whatever a dead party left. A Python-level profile hook turns every C call into a point where an asynchronous exception can skip the call; measured, about 7% of SIGALRM timeouts inside a section leak the harness's own `with lock:` under setprofile on 3.11-3.13. So v5f observes minted code through sys.monitoring local events on 3.12/3.13 (0 leaks, no cost outside targets), keeps setprofile on 3.11 with the timer-signal precondition refused, and refuses 3.10.

per_finding.how: Provenance now binds the CODE, not only the function object. A link of the declared object or of its own-dict __wrapped__ chain satisfies provenance iff both hold: (1) link.__globals__ is mod.__dict__; (2) link.__code__.co_filename, after realpath and normcase, equals mod.__file__ (a .pyc __file__ is compared without its trailing 'c'), or co_filename starts with '<' (exec-generated code in the module's own globals, e.g. dataclass __init__). A module with no str __file__ refuses FOREIGN_DEFINITION (fail closed, disclosed). The walk is bounded at 16 hops, cycle-detected and reads only C descriptors. Prototype p_prov.py on 3.11-3.13: the round-4 shape B (real.__code__ = stub.__code__) and shape C (FunctionType(stub.__code__, vars(mod))) both refuse. Plain functions, dataclass __init__, foreign wraps chains and the P1 .txt SourceFileLoader shape are admitted. New exam cases: X26b (shape B, before the trace) and X26c (shape C), both FOREIGN_DEFINITION. L-STUB is rewritten to say provenance proves which globals and which source file the code was compiled from. It adds residual R05b: a stub with a forged co_filename, or '<'-compiled code exec'd into the module's globals, passes (deliberate only). The J1-X1 closure row is corrected.

The machinery contains no threading lock at all. Enter and exit exclude each other through a robust mutex: a succession chain of transaction tokens (tid, id(frame), code, succ-dict). Acquire is `last.succ.setdefault('next', me) is me`, one C op. A token is live only if its frame is on sys._current_frames()[tid]'s f_back chain AND that frame's local `me` IS the token. A dead owner's slot is claimed by the next acquirer. A live owner on the same thread refuses REENTRANT, and a live foreign owner held for more than 10 s refuses MACHINERY_BUSY. A skipped release (a profiled C call, a signal, a hook raising) therefore never blocks anyone. _open and _close take no mutex at all. On 3.12/3.13 the monitoring adapter never runs at a C call. Prototype, on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13: an exception injected at every machinery bytecode caused 0 hangs; the SIGALRM sweep, nested inside an outer tracer with a worker-thread probe every 50 cycles, ran 117k-233k cycles with 26k-50k timeouts, 0 mutex holds left and 0 worker hangs. The v5e-style `with RLock` variant (M1) hangs the sweep. The same mechanism in USER code, where a hook raising at a c_call skips the user's own lock release, is a separate disclosure (L-SIGNAL-311).

For a C lru_cache/cache wrapper, F_T is the wrapper's real callee: the unique FunctionType among gc.get_referents(wrapper), which is the C `func` slot, verified identical on 3.10-3.13 by p_cache_callee.py. Resolution refuses NOT_A_FUNCTION ('__wrapped__ was restamped: it is not the function the wrapper calls') unless that callee IS the wrapper's own-dict __wrapped__. The bound-body refusal and the provenance walk both use the real callee. New exam cases: X24b (the wraps-over-lru_cache restamp from the repro) and X24c (the module-level reference variant, whose message must no longer name the wrong function), both NOT_A_FUNCTION. Spec step 4, L-CACHE and the 'nothing is unwrapped' sentence are corrected.

A generator, coroutine or async-generator target is credited per resumption that ran body bytecode. On 3.12/3.13 the monitoring adapter credits only PY_START and PY_RESUME. throw() and close() fire only PY_THROW, never credited: p_mon_gen.py shows 0 starts for dropped, closed or thrown unstarted generators and for close at a bare yield. On 3.11 the setprofile adapter stores frame.f_lasti at the frame's 'call' event in a per-thread pend dict (single writer, cleared at the thread's last close). It credits at the paired 'return' only if f_lasti moved. p_gen_progress.py on 3.10-3.13 confirms: dropped, closed or thrown unstarted generators and coroutines, and close at a bare yield, are never credited; consuming a 2-yield generator counts 3; asyncio.run counts. 3.10 is refused anyway. New exam case X119 pins these shapes to NOT_EXERCISED on every supported version. Versions and Stated limits now describe resumption counts: they are lower bounds, and a throw-resumption with a handler is counted on 3.11 only.

The dispatch cut becomes a monotone identity set _CUT (id(code) -> code). It holds every asyncio.events.Handle._run code object ever seen: captured at styxx.protocol import and again at each __enter__ BEFORE resolution, from vars(asyncio.events.Handle)['_run'], which must be a FunctionType or __enter__ refuses CUT_UNAVAILABLE. The set is never replaced or cleared, so _STOP and its reset at _ACTIVE == 0 are gone. asyncio.events:Handle._run, or any target whose code is in _CUT, refuses the new code RESERVED_TARGET at resolution, so the cut is never minted. A new exit tripwire CUT_MOVED (recorded) fires if vars(Handle)['_run'] is not a function whose code is in _CUT. The hook and the NESTED walk test `_CUT.get(id(f.f_code)) is f.f_code`. Exam cases: X34 (declaring Handle._run gives RESERVED_TARGET), X65b (the stop-cleared composite) and V44 (a `_run`-named helper). Spec lines 155 and 201 are corrected.

__enter__ refuses UNSUPPORTED_VERSION when sys.version_info < (3, 11). It is raised after the entry claim and before anything global is touched, so the tracer is dead and record() gives TRACE_INCOMPLETE. The reason: on 3.10, call_trampoline's FastToLocals/LocalsToFast around every Python profile callback reverts closure writes and keeps deleted locals alive, and no Python-level hook avoids it. My prototype also found a second 3.10-only hazard: importlib.import_module takes a module lock even for loaded modules on 3.10, and under SIGALRM with the hook installed its release is skipped, hanging worker threads (8/8 probes hung). Versions and Scope now read 3.11-3.13, the '3.9 expected like 3.10' line is deleted, and the 'R3 nit: f_locals cost' closure is marked 3.11+ only. Disclosed as over-blocking.

The rule is kept, because it fails closed. 'Sections are calls' and over-blocking #1/#4 now say that under asyncio.eager_task_factory (3.12+), a child task created on the stack of an open opening runs its first synchronous step on that stack. A section opened in that step is same-stack nesting and refuses NESTED_SECTION for the whole trace. The remedy is `await asyncio.sleep(0)` before cov.run_async, or no eager factory. New version-keyed exam cases (>=3.12): X83 expects NESTED_SECTION, and V35 shows the sleep(0) remedy scoring PASS with exact counts. Task-aware NESTED was rejected: it would add an asyncio.current_task dependency to _open and a rule change nobody needs for soundness.

This fails closed. When the refcount gate fires and gc.get_referrers finds no FunctionType holder while gc.get_freeze_count() > 0, exit counts the references to M_T held by VISIBLE referrers other than the mint and F_T. It records CLONE_ALIVE ('gc is frozen: N references are unscannable') if refcount - expected - visible > 0. Prototype t_freeze.py on 3.11-3.13: a clone frozen after creation refuses CLONE_ALIVE, a benign gc.freeze() inside a section passes, and a live generator of T frozen inside the section refuses. That last shape is the disclosed over-block. New exam cases: X57b (freeze with a live clone gives CLONE_ALIVE) and V36 (freeze with no clone gives PASS). The tripwire bullet and L-CLONE text are amended.

The FOREIGN_DEFINITION message follows the own-dict __wrapped__ chain (the same bounded, cycle-detected, descriptor-only walk) to its innermost FunctionType or real cache callee. It names `dict.get(inner.__globals__, '__name__') + ':' + inner.__qualname__` as 'declare this instead', and keeps the file path as a fallback. No user code runs, because __globals__ is read with dict.get and __qualname__ is a C member. Exam X29b checks that the message contains the defining module:qualname. The closure row is corrected.

Over-blocking #14 is rewritten. Code a trace or profile callback runs directly is never credited. Code it runs through sys.call_tracing (pdb's `debug` command) runs with events re-enabled and is credited to the section whose stack it lands on, like L-RUNTIME. That is observed on 3.12/3.13, and on all versions when the callback installs a nested tracer. It does not happen on 3.11, where call_tracing does not re-enable profiling. The shape joins the L-RUNTIME list and is pinned as version-keyed residual R12, which must be re-measured under the monitoring adapter before the freeze. A code fix is not possible: a callback frame cannot be told apart in general.

A finiteness helper `_finite(v)` returns False for an exact int too large for a double. It catches OverflowError only, never Exception, so asynchronous exceptions still propagate. check_metrics reports usable False with the note 'int too large for a float'. score() raises GateSpecError('gate G: metric ... is too large for a float') instead of OverflowError. The smoke flag is read as dict.get(result, 'smoke') and counts as truthy only for exact bool, int, float or str, so a user __bool__ never runs. Exam cases: X117b (a 400-digit int gives REPORTED from check_metrics and a GateSpecError from score) and X117c (a smoke object whose __bool__ raises gives REPORTED).

Aliases are accepted only when the declared OBJECTS are identical. Two declared names that resolve to one F_T through different declared objects refuse NOT_A_FUNCTION ('two different cache wrappers of one body are declared; declare the body'). The bound-body check also refuses when vars(mod) or the holder namespace contains another _CACHE_WRAPPER whose real callee is the body. The remaining case, a sibling wrapper held elsewhere, is disclosed in L-CACHE as 'every execution of the body counts, whatever route reaches it', pinned as residual R13 (sibling called, other declared: PASS). The 'no two distinct callables map to one code object' sentence gets the L-CACHE exception. Exam cases: X24d (both wrappers declared) and X24e (sibling in the same module), both NOT_A_FUNCTION.

There is no global _ACTIVE counter any more: the hook's self-removal uses the thread's opening set, and the cut is monotone. The exit claim `marks.setdefault('exiting', token)` is __exit__'s first statement. A tracer whose exit never began, because an exception landed at __exit__'s RESUME or at its 'call' event, is a zombie: record() refuses TRACE_ACTIVE, it can still run sections, and its mints stay installed (equal code). It is pruned at the next mutex acquisition once its facade is unreachable, which is detected by a callback-free weakref.ref(facade). The first prototype used weakref.finalize, and the SIGALRM sweep interrupted it before it could run ('Exception ignored in finalize'). Frames retained by the registries never reference the facade: marks hold frame-free tokens, and anchors are frames of module-level functions that take the core. The residual 'facade kept alive' is disclosed as L-ZOMBIE, and spec lines 262 and 504 are corrected.

The module registers os.register_at_fork(after_in_child=_forget_in_child). The handler sets _PID, retires every mint (restoring the original if installed and clearing its local monitoring events), clears _BY_FN, _MINTED, _ANCHORS and _TH, resets the mutex chain, and removes the hook if it is ours (3.11). The monitoring tool id is kept, being monotone. Every core records its pid. In another pid, _open returns None, so run() and run_async() just call fn: no section, no credit, no refusal. The robust mutex also heals by itself in a child, because an owner thread absent there counts as dead. Prototype t_lifecycle.py on 3.11-3.13: fork ProcessPoolExecutor jobs that call COV.run('B', g) return normally with no hook, no anchors and original code, and the parent trace has no problems. Over-block #15 is reworded, and the 'bootstrap frame' sentence and the R2-B3 closure are limited to threads. Exam case V47 (fork pool inside a section: parent PASS, children pass through).

Crediting frames that run T's ORIGINAL code would reopen R1-B1 and X48, because factory siblings and pre-trace clones share that code. Over-blocking #12 therefore gains: 'a generator, coroutine or async-generator OBJECT of T created before the trace (or in an earlier trace) keeps T's original code, so its frames are never credited, even when resumed inside a section; create it inside the trace (its callees are still credited)'. L-WHERE's generator example is narrowed to objects created during the trace. The NOT_EXERCISED fixed sentence gains 'generator and coroutine objects created before the trace are never credited'. Pinned as residual R14 (NOT_EXERCISED).

_check_coverage accepts any result for which issubclass(type(result), dict) holds, and still reads it with dict.get, so no subclass get or __missing__ runs. The NO_TRACE message is split into 'no coverage_trace key' and 'coverage_trace is a <type>, not an exact dict (e.g. loaded with object_pairs_hook)'. check_metrics' `present` uses the same test. Exam cases: X93c (a defaultdict result carrying the exact-dict record gives PASS) and X93d (an OrderedDict-loaded trace gives NO_TRACE with the second wording).

On the 3.11 adapter, both the hook's self-removal and the close and exit removals run only `if sys.getprofile() is _hook`, so a profiler that forwards events to our hook is never removed. The PROFILER_LOST note now reads 'the hook was not installed at close; calls after that may not have been observed'. On 3.12/3.13 there is no profile hook, so the finding is moot. Prototype t_func.py (4 versions): a chaining profiler started in a section stays installed and the forwarded target call is counted. New exam case V37 (3.11 keyed) checks it; it is 3.12+ trivially.

The provenance walk steps through the own-dict __wrapped__ of ANY link. The own dict is read through the GetSetDescriptor found in type(link)'s MRO, so no user code runs; a user-defined __dict__ stops the walk. The walk stays bounded at 16 hops and cycle-detected. Only a FunctionType link that passes the globals+file rule can satisfy provenance, and the minted object is still the one bound at the name, so there is no new over-credit route beyond L-STUB/R06. Prototype p_prov.py: `@logged @Memo def fit` is admitted on 3.11-3.13. New exam case V38 (wraps over class-based wrapper: {fit:1}) and a mutation row.

_open normalises a section whose type is a str subclass with str.__str__(section), the C slot, giving an exact str and never 'Sec.G'. A non-str section refuses UNDECLARED_SECTION without being compared, so no user __eq__ runs. Every section key in the record is therefore an exact str. Exam cases: V39 (StrEnum, numpy.str_-like and (str, Enum) sections give PASS) and X78f (an int section gives UNDECLARED_SECTION).

_check_trace_shape tests `type(o['end']) is not str or o['end'] not in _ENDS`, type check first, so membership is never evaluated for an unhashable value. Exam case X103b: end as a list or a dict gives BAD_TRACE from score, and REPORTED from check_metrics without raising.

Every enter and exit transaction starts with _reconcile() under the mutex. It prunes holders that are not live: facade collected, marked 'exited', another pid, a dead entering token with no 'active' mark, or a dead exiting token. Every mint left with no live holder is retired idempotently: restore only if fn.__code__ is m.code, then pop both registries, each step checked by identity. The entry-time CODE_SWAPPED check therefore sees only mints that live tracers hold. Prototype crash sweep invariants C3 (a fresh trace on another thread gives the baseline verdicts) and C5/C7 (registries hold only live holders, and everything is empty once facades are dropped) hold at every injection point on 3.10-3.13. New exam case X92b: a fault between restore and unregister, then a later trace of the same target must PASS.

check_metrics reports 'smoke run' only when the trace is ABSENT, mirroring the v3 rule. Otherwise the note is 'smoke run (score(smoke=True) does not read coverage): ' + str(e). Exam case X117d: a smoke result whose trace refuses NOT_EXERCISED must carry a note containing [V5:NOT_EXERCISED].

Own-dict reads on class, module and instance steps, on the provenance walk and on cache wrappers use C descriptors that cannot raise for valid objects: ModuleType.__dict__['__dict__'], type.__dict__['__dict__'/'__mro__'] and the instance GetSetDescriptor. They have no try, so an asynchronous exception propagates. The only `except Exception` sites left are the import of the declared module and the module's PEP 562 __getattr__, where arbitrary user code runs. There an asynchronous Exception subclass becomes a chained UNRESOLVED refusal, which is disclosed in L-ASYNC-EXC. The harness remedy is to import declared modules before the trace.

The per-thread registry is _TH[tid] = _ThreadRec(openings: set, epoch, pend). There are no counters: membership changes by idempotent set add and discard. An opening is finalised by ONE claim, `o.fin.setdefault('fin', (end, notes))`, followed by unconditional idempotent cleanups: pop the anchor keyed by the frame object, discard from the thread set, remove the hook on the opener thread when its set is empty (3.11), and clear o.frame. Exit detaches all of its openings on every thread whatever their state, and reconciliation does the same for pruned tracers. _open appends to core.openings, then adds to the thread set, then installs the hook, and registers the anchor LAST. The prototype crash sweep, which includes a coroutine section abandoned on a helper thread, leaves thread_openings = 0 and no hook on 3.10-3.13. The counter-style variant M8 is detected. L-ASYNC-EXC now states the envelope: end may read 'open' or 'raised', and notes may gain OPEN_AT_EXIT or PROFILER_LOST.

The cut and Handle._run are validated before resolution. asyncio is imported at module load; imports inside a transition are forbidden. The prototype showed that an interrupted `import asyncio.events` inside __enter__ leaves importlib's module lock held on 3.11. The entry claim makes a tracer single-use, so a retry refuses REENTRY. Inside the transaction a mint is registered with the core as holder BEFORE fn.__code__ is assigned, and local monitoring events are set before install. A failed or abandoned enter leaves a dead entering token, and the next reconciliation prunes it and retires its mints. Prototype t_lifecycle.py on 3.11-3.13: a MagicMock Handle._run refuses CUT_UNAVAILABLE with nothing minted. An audit hook refusing g's __code__ write mid-mint makes enter raise; a retry gives REENTRY and record() gives TRACE_INCOMPLETE; a later trace passes, registries are empty and every code object is restored. The spec gains 'Interrupted enter' next to 'Interrupted exit'.

The PEP 562 branch calls the module's __getattr__(part) twice. If the two products differ (`is not`), resolution refuses NOT_A_FUNCTION: 'module __getattr__ returns a new object on each access; declare the function it forwards to'. Products are never credited by constant code, which would reopen R3-B1. Over-blocking #8 and #9, the R3 PEP 562 closure row and Resolution step 2 ('called twice') are updated. New exam case X13b (deprecation shim gives NOT_A_FUNCTION).

The first statement of __enter__ is the atomic claim `core.marks.setdefault('entering', token) is token`. Exactly one caller wins; every other caller refuses REENTRY, which is always recorded into problems. The claim happens before the (GIL-releasing) imports and resolution, and no lock is held across them. Prototype t_lifecycle.py: 50/50 barrier-synchronised double entries give exactly one entry and exact counts on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13. New exam case X32d (a concurrent double enter: one entry, REENTRY recorded, counts exact) with its mutant (the claim replaced by a check-then-set).

Resolution branches on the real type, never obj.__class__: issubclass(type(obj), types.ModuleType), issubclass(type(obj), type), and type(obj) in (staticmethod, classmethod). Class internals are read with type.__dict__['__dict__'/'__mro__'/'__qualname__'].__get__(cls), the module dict with ModuleType.__dict__['__dict__'].__get__(mod), and the instance dict through the GetSetDescriptor from type(obj)'s MRO (a user-defined __dict__ gives INSTANCE_PATH). Probe p_resolve_c.py on 3.11-3.13: a strict registry whose __getattribute__ raises KeyError, a metaclass __getattribute__, a property __dict__ and a module subclass all resolve or refuse with no user code run. The docstring and the R1-D2 closure row are corrected. New exam case V40 (strict namespace gives PASS like V08).

New violation cases X07b (`section: ""`) and X07c (`section: "sеction"` with a Cyrillic е), both SECTION_DECL, plus mutation-audit row 'SECTION_DECL non-empty / ASCII clauses | X07b / X07c'. The refusal-deletion gate's region is widened to Experiment.__init__'s v5 block.

New case X57c: nested tracers on f. The inner section calls only a same-globals clone of M_T, kept alive past the inner exit and dropped before the outer exit, and the INNER trace must refuse CLONE_ALIVE. The mechanism already scans every mint the exiting tracer held, not only when the mint is released, and the SM1 catalog carries the 'only the last holder' weakening.
New case X55d: nested tracers on f. FunctionType(f.__code__, {})(1) runs while both hold the mint, and BOTH traces must refuse CLONE_CALLED. The shared _credit path marks every holder.

New case X59c: nested tracers. The inner section calls f, then swaps f.__code__ and leaves the swap in place through the inner exit, restoring it before the outer exit. The INNER trace must refuse CODE_SWAPPED; _exit_txn evaluates CODE_SWAPPED for every mint the exiting core holds.

The rule it guarded is replaced by a monotone cut captured before resolution, and Handle._run can no longer be minted. X34 (declaring asyncio.events:Handle._run gives RESERVED_TARGET) pins the refusal. The per-case leftover check gains the invariant `_CUT.get(id(H)) is H` for H = Handle._run.__code__ during and after every case, and the SM1 catalog carries 'cut read after a mint' and 'cut replaced instead of extended'.

New violation case X120: gate A declares f, gate B declares g; cov.run('A', g) then cov.run('B', f). A must refuse NOT_EXERCISED. New valid case V41: gates A and B both declare f and each section calls f once, so each union is exactly {f:1}, never {f:2}.

New valid cases V42 (G_fast[f] and G_slow[g] share section 'run'; one cov.run('run') calls both; PASS with exact unions) and V43 (a gate whose section is 'harness', not its name). New violation case X121 (X[f] with section 'Y', Y[g] with section 'X', the harness opening by gate name) must refuse NOT_EXERCISED. X78g opens a gate NAME that is not a declared section and must refuse UNDECLARED_SECTION; this kills the open-side sibling mutant.

New valid case V44: cov.run('G', _run, 1) with `def _run(cfg): return f() + cfg` in the fixture must score PASS {f:1}, which pins identity, not name, for the cut. The SM1 catalog carries 'cut by co_name'.

New valid case V11c: the declared target sits exactly 16 hops down a foreign functools.wraps chain and must score PASS. Paired with X30b (17 hops gives FOREIGN_DEFINITION), it pins the bound exactly and kills both range(3) and the off-by-one range(16).
