New valid case V45: methods of an abc.ABC subclass and of an Enum give PASS {target:1}. New violation case X14b: an inherited method of an ABC subclass gives INHERITED. The mechanism uses issubclass(type(obj), type).

New valid case V10b: the fixture sets sys.modules[__name__].__class__ to a ModuleType subclass and serves the target only through PEP 562 __getattr__, and must score PASS. X16b: a submodule of that class reached after the colon still refuses INSTANCE_PATH.
New violation case X14c: Leaf(Mid(Base)).fit and Model(LoggingMixin, Base).fit must refuse INHERITED (not UNRESOLVED), with the message 'declare the defining class'.

New violation cases X25c (Scorer.fast = staticmethod(lru_cache(None)(_impl)) with _impl bound at module level) and X25d (a wrapper served only through PEP 562, holder None, whose body is module-level). Both must refuse NOT_A_FUNCTION at entry.

New cases X122 (a declaring gate whose bar fails, m=0.0, and whose harness never calls one declared target must refuse NOT_EXERCISED, never return the table's FAIL row) and X122b (the same with a swallowed NESTED_SECTION must refuse NESTED_SECTION). The exam's _res() helper gains a failing-bar variant.

New case X96c: a genuine trace with gates_sha256 popped must refuse BAD_TRACE, never KeyError or STALE_TRACE. New case X78e: a harness that swallows cov.run('G_typo', f) and never opens G's section must refuse UNDECLARED_SECTION, not SECTION_ABSENT. The SM gate's O14 step-order operator targets every adjacent pair of score steps.

X72b asserts that the NOT_EXERCISED message contains the exact substring "dispatched {'<fx>:f': 2}, unattributed {}" on X72's trace, with each count under its own label. It also asserts check_metrics on that result gives G:exercises usable False and a note starting with [V5:NOT_EXERCISED]; X117d covers the smoke variant. The SM2 differential probe flags any future unasserted observable text difference as an EXAM_HOLE.

No clearing exists any more, because the cut is monotone. New case X65b: V15's inner tracer is entered and exited inside the outer; then section A of the outer runs an event loop serving another thread's run_coroutine_threadsafe and call_soon_threadsafe jobs. A must refuse NOT_EXERCISED with dispatched {f:2}.

New valid case V15b: an outer and an inner prereg both name their gate and section 'G', nested on one stack; both must score PASS {f:1}. A second variant uses a case section whose name equals the exam's self-trace section name.

X59d: after the trace exits and before the case's own finally restores the code, assert f59.__code__ is u59.__code__ (the swap is left in place) and f59() returns -59. _retire restores only `if fn.__code__ is m.code`.

X80c, keyed to 3.11: on a case-owned sub-thread, cov.run('G', body) where body calls f and then sys.setprofile(prof). After run returns, sys.getprofile() must be prof and the opening must carry PROFILER_LOST. On 3.12+ the expected outcome is prof installed with no note, because the monitoring adapter never touches profilers.

X80d: a case-owned sub-thread with no other openings runs an entire `with coverage_trace(exp)` and installs a pure-Python profiler inside the with, after its sections. After exit, sys.getprofile() on that thread must be that profiler. In v5f the exit removes the hook only if the exiting thread's set is empty and the hook is ours, so this is testable inside the self-trace, unlike v5e's _ACTIVE==0 block.

X32c: an explicit cov.__exit__() on success plus another in a finally, and __exit__ in a finally after __enter__ raised UNRESOLVED. That trace must score PASS {f:1}, a later independent trace must pass, and the leftovers must be clean. The exit claim `marks.setdefault('exiting', tok)` makes every second exit a no-op by construction, and the SM1 catalog carries 'claim replaced by an unconditional store'.

V28b, keyed to 3.11: coroutine section B opens on a worker thread and suspends; inside section A on the main thread the harness resumes B to completion (a THREAD_HOP close) and then calls A's target. Expected: A {f:1} with no PROFILER_LOST, B with a THREAD_HOP note. _detach removes a hook only when closer tid == opener tid.

X80e, keyed to 3.11: two run_async sections gathered on one loop; task a installs a pure-Python profiler before B opens. B must raise FOREIGN_PROFILER, recorded. On 3.12+ the expected outcome is PASS, since profilers coexist.
X109b: an old trace scored against a gates block that also adds a declared target (both gates_sha256 and the target set differ) must refuse STALE_TRACE.

X75b, keyed to 3.11: inside section G, call f, then sys.setprofile(p) with a pure-Python p, then call g; remove p after the close. G's notes must contain PROFILER_LOST and the NOT_EXERCISED message for g must name it.
X103c: a genuine one-opening trace with end replaced by class S(str) instance S('returned') must refuse BAD_TRACE. X103b covers the unhashable variants.
X112b: a trace carrying a genuine recorded problem (a swallowed UNDECLARED_SECTION) with one calls count set to 0 must refuse BAD_COUNT, not the problem's code.

V46: two threads, alive at once, each open a section and each dispatch g once through their own event loop's call_soon. record()['uncredited']['dispatched'] must equal {g: 2}, and the NOT_EXERCISED message for a gate declaring g must print 2.

The NESTED_SECTION reason now reads 'a call there would be on the stack of two openings of this trace' when o.section == section, and 'one call would count for both sections' otherwise. LAZY_RESULT is only emitted for exact generator, coroutine or async-generator result types (no isinstance, so no user __class__ runs). It now reads 'fn returned a <type>; whatever of its body runs after the section closed does not count', with ' (its body had not started)' appended when the object is in the created state. Mechanism comment line 213 is fixed. X76b and X74d pin both texts.

designs_all.mechanism_changes:
This builds on v5e mint-and-anchor. Identity (minting, the f_globals test, the tripwires) and attribution (the anchor walk, the Handle._run cut, exactly one opening per tracer) are unchanged in meaning. What is replaced is the state machine and the event source. Numbered for implementation.

M0. Version and adapter gate (first thing after the entry claim; raised, not recorded).
Refuse UNSUPPORTED_VERSION unless sys.version_info[:2] is one of (3,11), (3,12), (3,13), and unless the build has the GIL (refuse when getattr(sys, '_is_gil_enabled', lambda: True)() is False). The atomicity argument below needs the GIL.
Adapter P (sys.setprofile) runs on 3.11; adapter M (sys.monitoring) runs on 3.12 and 3.13.
Tracer id becomes 'styxx.protocol.coverage_trace/3'. /2 traces refuse WRONG_TRACER.
`import asyncio.events` happens at styxx.protocol import. No import may run inside any transition: the prototype showed an interrupted import leaves an importlib module lock held.

M1. State: every piece of shared state is one of three kinds.
(a) A registry changed only by single GIL-atomic C operations.
(b) An immutable value replaced by one STORE.
(c) A monotone map changed only by setdefault.
The registries:
- _BY_FN: {fn: _Mint}. The key holds fn.
- _MINTED: {id(code): _Mint}. The mint holds the code.
- _ANCHORS: {anchor frame object: _Opening}. Frames hash by identity, and the key holds the frame, so an id is never reused.
- _TH: {tid: _ThreadRec(openings=set(), epoch, pend={})}.
- _CUT: {id(code): code}. Monotone: setdefault only, never cleared.
- _GUARD: {'hint': _Txn}, the head of the robust-mutex chain.
- _TOOL: [id or None]. Monotone on 3.12+.
_Mint(fn, original, code=original.replace(), globals, holders=()). holders is a TUPLE, rebuilt only under the mutex; the event path reads it lock-free.
_Core, one per tracer, is what the registries reference: exp; marks (a monotone dict holding 'entering'->_Txn, 'active'->True, 'exiting'->_Txn, 'exited'->True); by_code {id(code): names} (emptied first at exit); names (kept for record); openings (list); problems (list); clone_called (dict); uncredited {tid: ({}, {})}; facade (a weakref.ref with NO callback); pid.
The user-facing _CoverageTracer is a thin facade holding its core.
Every frame the machinery may retain belongs to a module-level function whose locals hold the core, never the facade: the anchor is _run's frame or _run_async's coroutine frame, and marks and mutex records hold frame-FREE _Txn tokens. The prototype showed that a retained dead frame keeps its whole f_back chain, and so the facade, alive.
_Txn(tid, fid=id(frame), code=frame.f_code, succ={}) is created by `me = _txn()`. It is live iff some frame f on sys._current_frames()[tid]'s f_back chain has id(f) == fid, f.f_code is code, and f.f_locals.get('me') is the token. This is exact, holds no frame, and needs no callback.

M2. Robust mutex (enter and exit only; _open, _close, the event path and record() never take it).
_locked(fn, *args): me = _txn(); _acquire(me); out = fn(*args); _release(me); return out. There is deliberately no try/finally.
_acquire walks from _GUARD['hint'] along succ['next'] to the last token r.
- If r is live and r.tid == me.tid: raise GateSpecError('[V5:REENTRANT] ...').
- If r is live on another thread: sleep 0.2 ms and retry; after 10 s raise '[V5:MACHINERY_BUSY] ...'.
- Otherwise (free or dead): claim with `r.succ.setdefault('next', me) is me`. If the claim won, store the hint; if it lost, re-walk.
_release: me.succ.setdefault('next', _Txn(None, 0, None)) (a free token).
A release skipped for any reason (a profiled C call, a signal, a hook raising) is harmless: the owner's frame dies with the exception and the next acquirer steals.

M3. Reconciliation (the first step of every transaction, under the mutex).
For every mint in _BY_FN ∪ _MINTED: keep = the live holders, where a holder is dead iff any of these holds:
- its facade weakref is dead;
- 'exited' is in marks;
- its pid differs from this process's;
- its 'exiting' token is dead;
- 'active' is absent and its 'entering' token is dead.
For each pruned holder h: set h.by_code = {} and _detach every opening of h with ('open', OPEN_AT_EXIT 'pruned: the trace's own exit did not run'). Then m.holders = keep.
If keep is empty, _retire(m), which is idempotent and consistent at every prefix:
- if fn.__code__ is m.code, restore m.original;
- (3.12+) set_local_events(tool, m.code, 0);
- pop _BY_FN if the value is m;
- pop _MINTED if the value is m.

M4. __enter__ (the facade calls _enter(core)).
E0. me = _txn(). If core.marks.setdefault('entering', me) is not me, append a REENTRY problem and raise REENTRY.
E1. M0 gate.
E2. h = vars(asyncio.events.Handle).get('_run'). If type(h) is not FunctionType, refuse CUT_UNAVAILABLE; otherwise _CUT.setdefault(id(h.__code__), h.__code__).
E3. Resolve every target (M8). A target whose F_T is h or whose code is in _CUT refuses RESERVED_TARGET. Aliases are allowed only when the declared objects are identical.
E4. _locked(_enter_txn, core, resolved), which runs, in order:
- reconcile;
- (3.12+) acquire a tool id (M6);
- for each distinct F_T: if a live mint exists and F_T.__code__ is not m.code, refuse CODE_SWAPPED (nothing joined yet);
- for each F_T: if it has a mint, m.holders = m.holders + (core,). Otherwise create it in this exact order: build m (pure); m.holders = (core,); _MINTED[id(m.code)] = m; _BY_FN[fn] = m; (3.12+) set_local_events(tool, m.code, PY_START|PY_RESUME); fn.__code__ = m.code;
- core.names = {...}; core.by_code = dict(core.names).
E5. core.marks['active'] = True, AFTER the mutex is released. Between release and this commit the entering token is live, so no reconciler prunes the core.
E6. Return.

M5. __exit__ (the facade calls _exit(core); it never raises GateSpecError).
X0. If 'active' is not in marks: _locked(_reconcile) and return. This completes any abandoned enter.
X1. me = _txn(). If core.marks.setdefault('exiting', me) is not me, return: a second exit is a no-op.
X2. core.by_code = {} (credit stops; one store).
X3. For o in list(core.openings): _detach(o, tid, ('open', (OPEN_AT_EXIT,))).
X4. probs = CLONE_CALLED entries from dict(core.clone_called).
X5. _locked(_exit_txn), which runs: reconcile (this core is exiting with a live token, so it is kept); then for every mint m holding core: append CODE_SWAPPED if m.fn.__code__ is not m.code; m.holders = tuple(h for h in m.holders if h is not core); _retire(m) if the tuple is empty. A GateSpecError from _locked (REENTRANT or MACHINERY_BUSY) is appended as a recorded problem and exit continues. The unreleased holdership is pruned later, because the exit token dies.
X6. For each mint the core held: the CLONE_ALIVE refcount gate. expected = 2 + (fn.__code__ is m.code). Scan gc.get_referrers only if the gate fires. Record CLONE_ALIVE if any FunctionType other than fn holds M_T, OR (gc.get_freeze_count() > 0 and refcount - expected - visible_refs_excluding_mint_and_fn > 0). Add the CUT_MOVED tripwire.
X7. core.problems.extend(probs) (one call). (3.11) If this thread's opening set is empty and sys.getprofile() is _hook, set the profile to None.
X8. core.marks['exited'] = True (commit).

M6. Event path.
The shared part, _credit(frame, code, m, tid):
- if frame.f_globals is not m.globals: set h.clone_called[id(code)] for every h in m.holders, and return;
- walk f = frame.f_back until the cut (`_CUT.get(id(f.f_code)) is f.f_code`) or the root, collecting _ANCHORS.get(f);
- for each holder h with id(code) in h.by_code, with `mine` being the found openings whose core is h: exactly one opening gets a single-key increment of o.calls[id(code)]; two or more each get an increment of ambiguous; none gets an increment of h.uncredited[tid][0 if cut else 1];
- names are expanded only in record().
Adapter M (3.12/3.13): tool id 3 or 4, whichever is free or already named 'styxx.protocol'; if neither, refuse MONITOR_BUSY. Once taken, the id is kept for the process lifetime (monotone). Callbacks are registered for PY_START and PY_RESUME only, and events are set LOCALLY on each minted code object. PY_THROW and PY_UNWIND are not used: throw() and close() fire only PY_THROW, so they are never credited. The callback: m = _MINTED.get(id(code)); require m and m.code is code; require the thread's opening set to be non-empty (diagnostics then see the same threads as 3.11); then _credit(sys._getframe(1), ...). No handler and no lock. An exception propagates, and the tool is not dropped. At exit, the new MONITOR_LOST note (never refuses) is added if get_tool(id) is no longer ours or a held mint's local events were cleared.
Adapter P (3.11) is the v5e hook, restructured:
- tr = _TH.get(tid); if tr is None or tr.openings is empty: remove the hook ONLY IF sys.getprofile() is _hook, and return;
- a 'return' event returns at once unless tr.pend is non-empty; events other than 'call' and 'return' return;
- identity check;
- generator, coroutine and async-generator code (co_flags & 0x3A0): at 'call', tr.pend[frame] = f_lasti; at 'return', credit only if the frame was pending and f_lasti moved. Other code is credited at 'call'.

M7. _open(core, section, anchor), lock-free (called from module-level _run(core, section, fn, args, kwargs), whose frame is the anchor, and from _run_async).
- If core.pid != this pid, return None; run then just calls fn (fork pass-through).
- Refusals, recorded when active: TRACE_INACTIVE; section normalisation (a str subclass becomes str.__str__(section); a non-str gives UNDECLARED_SECTION without comparing); UNDECLARED_SECTION; NESTED_SECTION, walking anchor.f_back to the cut and matching o.core is core; (3.11) FOREIGN_PROFILER; (3.11, main thread) SIGNAL_TIMER if signal.getsignal() of SIGALRM, SIGVTALRM or SIGPROF is a Python callable.
- tr = _TH.get(tid), or _TH.setdefault(tid, _ThreadRec()).
- ep = next(_EPOCH) if no profiler is installed, else tr.epoch.
- o = _Opening(...) (pure); core.openings.append(o); tr.openings.add(o); (3.11, no profiler installed) tr.epoch = ep and sys.setprofile(_hook); _ANCHORS[anchor] = o (the commit, last).
_close(o, end):
- compute notes (pure): THREAD_HOP if the closing tid is not o.tid; (3.11) PROFILER_LOST if the hook is not ours or the epoch changed; (3.11, main thread) a recorded SIGNAL_TIMER if a timer handler is present now;
- _detach(o, tid, (end, notes)), which runs: o.fin.setdefault('fin', value) (the claim and commit); _ANCHORS.pop(o.frame, None); tr.openings.discard(o); if the closer is the opener and the set is empty, tr.pend.clear() and (3.11) remove the hook if it is ours; o.frame = None.
- run() sets o.lazy only for an exact result type in {generator, coroutine, async generator}.

M8. Resolution and provenance. No user code runs except the import and a module's PEP 562 __getattr__. Those two keep `except Exception`, giving a chained UNRESOLVED; nothing else has a handler.
- Branch on issubclass(type(obj), ModuleType or type) and on type(obj) in (staticmethod, classmethod).
- Read dicts only through C descriptors (M2 of the per-finding notes).
- PEP 562: call __getattr__ twice; if the two products are not identical, refuse NOT_A_FUNCTION.
- Cache wrappers: F_T is the unique FunctionType in gc.get_referents(wrapper), and it must be the own-dict __wrapped__. Refuse NOT_A_FUNCTION if the body is bound by name, or if another cache wrapper of the same body is in vars(mod) or in the holder.
- Provenance: a FunctionType link with __globals__ is mod.__dict__ AND a co_filename matching mod.__file__ (or '<'-prefixed). The walk passes through any link's own-dict __wrapped__ (descriptor read), up to 16 hops, cycle-detected.
- The FOREIGN_DEFINITION message names the innermost module:qualname.

M9. record() is pure.
It needs 'exited' in marks. Otherwise it refuses TRACE_INCOMPLETE if 'exiting' is present, or if 'entering' is present without 'active'; else it refuses TRACE_ACTIVE.
An opening's end and notes come from o.fin (default ('open', ())), plus LAZY_RESULT. Counts are expanded through core.names. uncredited is summed across threads.
The recorded codes add CUT_MOVED, SIGNAL_TIMER, REENTRANT and MACHINERY_BUSY. The notes add MONITOR_LOST.

M10. at-fork: os.register_at_fork(after_in_child=...): set _PID; _retire every mint; clear _BY_FN, _MINTED, _ANCHORS and _TH; reset _GUARD; (3.11) remove the hook if it is ours.

M11. Scoring.
- _check_coverage accepts a dict subclass as the result (read with dict.get), with the split NO_TRACE message.
- _check_trace_shape tests the exact type before `end in _ENDS`.
- check_metrics: _finite catches OverflowError only; smoke is read with exact-type truthiness; 'smoke run' is used only when the trace is absent.
- score() turns an OverflowError from float() into a GateSpecError.
- All other score steps and their order are unchanged. Each step pair is pinned by the new cases.

M12. Deleted: _LOCK, _ACTIVE, _STOP, the _THREADS counts, and weakref.finalize. Every [V5:CODE] literal still sits at its own emission site (G7), and the refusal-deletion gate is converted to mutate by coded LITERAL (see the gate section).
designs_all.version_policy:
3.10: REFUSED at __enter__ with UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, before anything global is touched. On 3.10, call_trampoline wraps every Python-level profile callback in FastToLocals and LocalsToFast. That reverts closure writes made by other threads and keeps deleted locals alive (round-4 blocker). No pure-Python hook avoids it, and 3.10 has no sys.monitoring. The prototype also found that importlib.import_module takes a module lock even for loaded modules on 3.10, and under SIGALRM with the hook installed that lock's release is skipped: 8 of 8 worker probes hung. The spec deletes the '3.9 expected like 3.10' line. Disclosed as over-blocking.

3.11: SUPPORTED through adapter P (sys.setprofile), with the same state machine as every other version.
Behaviour specific to 3.11:
- FOREIGN_PROFILER and the PROFILER_LOST note (epochs) exist only here;
- generator credit uses the f_lasti progress rule;
- sys.call_tracing does not credit;
- NEW: SIGNAL_TIMER, a recorded refusal at open and at close on the main thread when a Python handler is installed for SIGALRM, SIGVTALRM or SIGPROF.
Why SIGNAL_TIMER: the hook makes each c_call a delivery point where CPython skips the call. Measured under SIGALRM on a `with lock:` loop inside a section, 3606 of 50385 timeouts leaked the harness's own lock, against 0 untraced (7%; the prototype's SIGNAL_TIMER check was not active in this run).
Ctrl-C is disclosed as the residual L-SIGNAL-311. 3.11 is kept because it is the lab's default interpreter (P1 retro, exam). Refusing it is the named alternative if the panel judges L-SIGNAL-311 a corruption on a par with py310.

3.12 and 3.13: SUPPORTED through adapter M (sys.monitoring). Tool id 3 or 4 is held for the process lifetime. Only PY_START and PY_RESUME are enabled, as LOCAL events on minted code objects. The callback never runs at a C call, so the profiled-C-call hazard class is closed structurally for user code as well as for the machinery. Measured: 0 lock leaks out of 51075 (3.12) and 52456 (3.13) timeouts; the setprofile adapter on the same interpreters leaked 3362 and 3553. It also costs nothing outside targets (x1.0 against x11-17 for setprofile on 1M non-target calls), is 2.5-3x cheaper per hit, and coexists with every sys.setprofile and sys.settrace tool (cProfile, profile, yappi, pyinstrument, pdb), so FOREIGN_PROFILER and PROFILER_LOST do not arise. MONITOR_BUSY refuses when tool ids 3 and 4 are both taken by other tools. throw() and close() fire only PY_THROW and are never credited. sys.call_tracing code is credited (L-RUNTIME, version-keyed).

3.14+ and free-threaded builds: REFUSED (UNSUPPORTED_VERSION) until re-validated. The atomicity argument assumes the GIL.

Why two adapters despite v5e's objection: the objection was the doubled exam matrix. Here one state machine, the reconciliation logic, the attribution walk and the crediting code are shared, and the adapter interface is one function, _credit(frame, code, m, tid). The version-keyed expectations are an enumerated list in the prereg: FOREIGN_PROFILER, PROFILER_LOST, SIGNAL_TIMER, MONITOR_BUSY, the throw-resumption count, call_tracing, eager tasks and cProfile. Every other case must be identical on 3.11-3.13. The aux gate's second implementation and the oracle fuzzer run on all three.
designs_all.new_limits_and_overblocking:
NEW OVER-BLOCKING, each a refusal of a legitimate harness, disclosed:
(1) 3.10 refuses UNSUPPORTED_VERSION entirely, as do 3.14+ and free-threaded builds.
(2) 3.11 only: SIGNAL_TIMER, recorded at open and at close on the main thread, when a Python handler for SIGALRM, SIGVTALRM or SIGPROF is installed. This covers pytest-timeout's signal method, signal.alarm budgets and the exam's own H2 shape on 3.11. Remedy: thread-based timeouts, or 3.12+.
(3) 3.12+: MONITOR_BUSY when other tools hold sys.monitoring ids 3 and 4. v5f holds its id for the process lifetime.
(4) RESERVED_TARGET: asyncio.events:Handle._run, and any function whose code is a recorded cut code.
(5) CUT_MOVED: a harness or library that rebinds Handle._run during a trace refuses every gate.
(6) CUT_UNAVAILABLE: Handle._run is not a plain function at enter (mocked or C-replaced).
(7) FOREIGN_DEFINITION now also refuses:
- modules without a str __file__ (in-memory modules);
- sourceless or relocated installs whose co_filename differs from __file__ (for example conda prefix relocation);
- targets whose __code__ was swapped before the trace (intended).
(8) NOT_A_FUNCTION now also refuses:
- a cache wrapper whose __wrapped__ is not its real callee;
- a PEP 562 attribute that returns a new object on each access (deprecation shims): declare the target;
- two different cache wrappers of one body declared, or held in the same namespace as the declared one.
(9) CLONE_ALIVE while gc is frozen: a frozen or untracked holder of M_T (a live generator or traceback of T frozen in the section) refuses.
(10) A tracer whose __enter__ raised is single-use: a retry refuses REENTRY. Create a new tracer.
(11) REENTRANT: a finalizer or signal handler that enters or exits a tracer during another enter or exit on the same thread.
(12) MACHINERY_BUSY: another thread holds enter or exit for more than 10 s.
(13) Eager tasks (3.12+): a child that opens its section in its first synchronous step refuses NESTED_SECTION for the whole trace. Remedy: await asyncio.sleep(0) first.
(14) Generator and coroutine targets: throw() and close() resumptions are never credited on 3.12+; on 3.11 they are credited only if the frame's f_lasti moved. Generator and coroutine objects created before the trace are never credited.
(15) Sections opened concurrently with the tracer's exit on another thread refuse TRACE_INACTIVE or record as 'open' with zero calls.

CHANGED OR NEW STATED LIMITS:
- L-SIGNAL-311 (new): on 3.11 only, while a section is open on a thread, an async exception can surface at any C call's c_call event, and CPython skips that call. A `with lock:` release (measured: about 7% of SIGALRM timeouts in a lock-dense loop) or an importlib module-lock release during a first-time import can leak, hanging other threads. SIGNAL_TIMER refuses the timer-signal precondition. Ctrl-C (SIGINT) is the remaining residual. 3.12+ is immune (0 of 51k).
- L-ZOMBIE (new): an exception at __exit__'s entry, or at __enter__'s return on a profiled thread, leaves an active tracer. record() refuses. Its minted (equal) code stays installed until the facade is unreachable and the next enter or exit reconciles. A double fault leaving a stale anchor can keep the facade reachable.
- L-ASYNC-EXC (rewritten as the envelope I6): any fault anywhere in the machinery can only lose counts or make a record read 'open', 'raised', OPEN_AT_EXIT or PROFILER_LOST, or make record() refuse. An async Exception landing in the declared module's import or in its PEP 562 __getattr__ becomes a chained UNRESOLVED.
- L-STUB (widened): provenance proves which globals and which source file the code was compiled from, not that it is the original binding. An in-module stub, a wraps-stamped stub, code with a forged co_filename, and '<'-compiled code exec'd into the module's globals are credited (R05, R06, R05b).
- L-CACHE (widened): every execution of the body counts, whatever route reaches it, including a sibling cache wrapper held outside the scanned namespaces (R13).
- L-WHERE (narrowed): generators and coroutines count only if created during the trace (R14).
- L-RUNTIME (widened): sys.call_tracing code (pdb debug) is credited on 3.12/3.13 and not on 3.11 (R12, version-keyed).
- Counts: resumption counts for generators are lower bounds and version-keyed for throw shapes.
- CPython only; GIL only; greenlet and gevent are untested. The robust mutex's liveness check assumes that a frame executing on a thread is reachable from that thread's current frame, which greenlet stack switching breaks.

REMOVED OVER-BLOCKING on 3.12+: pure-Python profilers, yappi, pyinstrument, profile and cProfile all coexist (FOREIGN_PROFILER no longer applies there). Hook loss through a harness's setprofile(None) or a RecursionError drop (#7) no longer applies. The per-event cost on non-target code (#17) is gone.
designs_all.risks:
WHAT COULD REOPEN ROUNDS 1-3, and the guard for each:
(1) R3-B3 (an exception swallowed in the hook): the monitoring callback must have no handler, and a callback exception propagates without dropping the tool (verified in p_mon.py). A round-5 red team should check RecursionError and KeyboardInterrupt raised inside PY_RESUME of a coroutine driven by asyncio's C Task.
(2) R1-B3/R2-B2/R3-B2 (class B): the monitoring adapter depends on sys._getframe(1) inside a PY_START/PY_RESUME callback being the target frame, with the true f_back chain. It was verified for plain calls, asyncio Handle._run and threads. Unverified: resumption from C (map(next, gens), itertools, the C Task step, contextvars.Context.run, sys.monitoring during another tool's callback). Attack this first on 3.12/3.13.
(3) R1-B1/R3-B1 (class A): minting is unchanged, but local events are set on M_T, so an in-trace clone of M_T fires them. That matches v5e's L-CLONE. A code.replace() copy of M_T gets no events and is never credited, which is correct.
(4) R1-D2 (resolution crashes and user code): the descriptor-only reads should be attacked with C-extension types, __slots__ plus __dict__ mixes, and module subclasses that override __dict__ as a descriptor.
(5) R2-B3 (the hook persists on a thread): on 3.11 a thread's hook stays only while its opening set is non-empty; a zombie's stale opening can keep an inert hook on a thread (L-ZOMBIE).
(6) R3-D3 (finalizer deadlock): there are no locks. The robust mutex refuses REENTRANT instead of waiting, and the event path takes nothing.

WHAT ROUND 5 SHOULD ATTACK FIRST:
(a) Divergence between the two adapters: run the whole exam and fuzzer on 3.11 against 3.12 and look for any outcome outside the enumerated version-keyed list, for example uncredited diagnostics or generator counts.
(b) The robust mutex. Exactness of liveness: a dead frame's id reused by a new frame of the same code, which the `me` identity rule defends. The cost of sys._current_frames() under contention. Exhausting the 10 s BUSY bound with a legitimately slow owner, since the enter transaction iterates all mints. Greenlet-style stack switching.
(c) The crash-sweep scope. The prototype injected on ONE scenario family on the main thread only; inject on two threads, into run_async and THREAD_HOP closes, and into generator targets. The lab's existing fault_injection_v5.py found 2547 of 10371 v5e points broken, 130 of them HANGs; it must be re-run on v5f through the monitoring injector.
(d) The false-refusal surface of provenance co_filename: symlinked checkouts, zipimport, editable installs, .pth-relocated trees, __file__ relative to cwd.
(e) L-ZOMBIE through module-level `cov` globals, and a double fault that leaves a stale anchor keeping the facade alive.
(f) The SIGNAL_TIMER precondition is incomplete: handlers installed and removed within a section, threading-based libraries that route through signal.pthread_kill.
(g) sys.monitoring interplay: another tool calling free_tool_id, restart_events or set_events on our id (the MONITOR_LOST note under-counts only), tool-id squatting, and bugs in 3.12.x instrumentation. The prototype hit a 3.12.3 settrace opcode bug, so re-validate per patch release.
(h) The noise mask and envelope in SM2 could hide a real regression if a field is nondeterministic in the baseline: the mask must be minimal and reported.
Deliberately not done, and the principal residual: 3.11 keeps the setprofile adapter. If the panel ranks L-SIGNAL-311 with py310, refusing 3.11 makes v5f single-adapter.

designs_all.name: v5f-narrow ("fence"): credit only what the mechanism can prove, and refuse every other shape at entry with a coded, remedy-bearing message
designs_all.thesis: v5f keeps v5e's mint-and-anchor core. Each round-4 hole is closed one of two ways: by an exact rule grounded in CPython 3.11-3.13 facts that were measured on four interpreters, or, where no such rule is provable, by refusing the shape at __enter__ with its own reason code and a working remedy (3.10, generator/coroutine targets, directly declared C cache wrappers, code not compiled from its module's file, asyncio, PEP 562 products not bound in the module). Every _LOCK region releases through the with-statement's exceptional path, which no profile hook can abort; every multi-step state change is ordered, idempotent and reconciled at the next enter or exit; and the exam is gated by a ledger of weakened-rule mutants, frozen before implementation, each bound to one named kill case that isolates its clause.

per_finding.how: Provenance now ties the code object to the module. Rule CF1: F_T must satisfy code.co_filename == dict.get(F_T.__globals__,'__file__'), both exact str, and code whose filename starts with '<' refuses. Rule CF2: the accepting __wrapped__ link must pass the same check against the declared module. The refusal is FOREIGN_DEFINITION and names module:co_qualname plus the file. Prototype: the verifier's variants B (f.__code__ = stub.__code__) and C (FunctionType(stub code, vars(mod))) refuse at entry on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, and the baseline still passes. Cases K_pretrace_code_swap, K_pretrace_swap_on_wrapper (CF1) and K_pretrace_swap_inner_link (CF2). Residual, moved into L-STUB: a stub compiled from the module's own file, a wraps-stamped stub, and a forged co_filename (code.replace), which only a deliberate harness would build.

Every `with _LOCK:` body ends with `raise _Release` (a private BaseException), which is caught immediately outside. RLock.__exit__ is then called by the with-statement's exceptional path (WITH_EXCEPT_START), which is never reported to a profile function; a normal exit calls it through CALL, whose c_call event a raising hook can abort. The event lists were measured identical on 3.10.20/3.11.15/3.12.3/3.13.12: plain `with` orphaned the lock in 1 of 10 raise positions, the v5f shape in 0 of 8. The verifier's SIGALRM repro ran 45 s per version and exception kind (Timeout and KeyboardInterrupt), about 75-80k real exceptions each, and the lock was never orphaned on 3.11, 3.12 or 3.13; unmodified v5e hung a worker within 15 s. Ledger row LOCK, killed by K_lock_release_under_raising_hook: module-global _hook rebound to raise at each c_call of a nested _open; the v5e-shape mutant orphans the lock at k=2.

A C lru_cache/cache wrapper is no longer a declarable object. It refuses NOT_A_FUNCTION with the remedy spelled out: declare the own-dict path 'module:name.__wrapped__', which the existing instance step already resolves to the body. The declaration then literally names what is minted, so identity never rests on an implicit __wrapped__ read. staticmethod/classmethod are unwrapped (C __func__ member) at every path step, so 'mod:C.m.__wrapped__' works for class-held caches. This removes the v5e cache-body branch entirely. Prototype: the verifier's re-stamped repro refuses at entry; the remedy counts a miss {cached.__wrapped__:1} and a hit reads NOT_EXERCISED (battery 27/27 on 3.11-3.13).

Any F_T whose co_flags carry CO_GENERATOR, CO_COROUTINE, CO_ITERABLE_COROUTINE or CO_ASYNC_GENERATOR refuses GENERATOR_TARGET at entry. setprofile reports close(), throw() and drop of an unstarted or bare-yield frame as 'call', differently per version, and no profile event can tell those from a run (checked: f_lasti is identical at call time). The remedy is to declare a plain function the body calls. 3.10 is also refused (UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME). Prototype: the verifier's my_repro refuses at entry. Ledger row GEN, killed by K_generator_refused.

RESERVED_TARGET refuses two things: any target whose module is 'asyncio' or 'asyncio.*' (checked before the import), and any F_T whose __code__ is the dispatch-cut code (checked by identity, which catches a sys.modules alias of asyncio.events). The cut code is read at the start of __enter__, before resolution. It is never minted and never cleared at exit, so no tracer can make it stale. Prototype: the verifier's v_repro refuses at entry. Ledger rows RES1 (K_asyncio_other_function) and RES2 (K_asyncio_cut_via_alias), both killed.

__enter__ refuses UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME unless sys.version_info[:2] is in {(3,11),(3,12),(3,13)} and sys._is_gil_enabled() is not False. On 3.10, CPython's call_trampoline runs FastToLocals/LocalsToFast around every Python-level profile callback. That corrupts the traced program, and no pure-Python hook can avoid it. Prototype: the verifier's own_repro on 3.10.20 raises UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME at entry. The '3.9 expected like 3.10' sentence is deleted.

os.register_at_fork(after_in_child=...) resets a forked child: a fresh _LOCK (the parent's may be held); minted code restored; _MINTED, _BY_FN, _ANCHORS, _THREADS and _LIVE cleared; every inherited tracer set to state 'forked'; our hook removed. cov.run in a child then raises TRACE_INACTIVE ('forked'), loud and early; child work was never credited and still is not. Spec'd but not prototyped: a tracer _pid check in _open, for forks that skip the at-fork handlers. Prototype (verifier's v_fork_pool, 3.11): the C1, C2 and C5 jobs raise TRACE_INACTIVE 'forked'; the parent scores A {f:1} and B SECTION_ABSENT; the idle C4 worker has no hook, empty registries and no slowdown (0.0157 vs 0.0156 s). Ledger row FORK (K_fork_child_forgets) killed. The 'bootstrap frame' sentence is limited to threads.

Generator, coroutine and async-generator functions are not declarable (GENERATOR_TARGET), so there is no declared generator whose pre-trace objects could be silently uncredited. A plain target called from inside such an object's body is an ordinary call and is credited where it runs (L-WHERE). Prototype: the verifier's script refuses at entry. The sentences 'counts are frame entries' and 'generator resumptions count again' are deleted: counts are calls.

_check_coverage reads the trace with issubclass(type(result), dict) and dict.get, so no user __class__, get or __missing__ runs. The NO_TRACE message is split three ways: not a dict; no 'coverage_trace' key; a <type> that is not an exact dict. check_metrics' 'present' uses the same test. Prototype: bare subclass, defaultdict and OrderedDict all PASS with {g:1}.

The hook's self-removal is guarded by `if sys.getprofile() is _hook`; a profiler that chains to the hook is never removed. PROFILER_LOST now reads 'may not have been observed'. Over-blocking #6 gains: a profiler that forwards to the hook keeps the section counted and stays installed. Prototype: chain_all and chain_py stay installed, see 5/5 later calls and PASS; a battery case confirms this on 3.11-3.13.

The provenance walk (provenance only, never identity) now steps through the own-dict __wrapped__ of any object. The own __dict__ is read only through the type's C __dict__ descriptor (getset or member; a Python-level __dict__ property stops the walk). Cycle detection is dropped: the 16-hop bound terminates every walk, so the minimal mechanism suffices. This adds no false-PASS route beyond L-STUB, because what is minted is still the declared FunctionType bound at the name. The class-based wrapper itself as the declared object still refuses NOT_A_FUNCTION. Prototype: `@logged @memoize def fit` PASSes; memoize alone refuses NOT_A_FUNCTION. Ledger rows P01, P02 and P03 pin the bound from both sides (K_hop_16_accepted, K_hop_17_refused).

_open normalizes a str subclass (StrEnum, str-mixin Enum, numpy.str_) by value with str.__str__ before any check. A non-str section refuses UNDECLARED_SECTION by exact type, so a user __eq__ never runs in the membership test. Prototype: every spelling and both orders PASS with the key 'G'; an int section refuses UNDECLARED_SECTION.

Rule: every comparison and every hash in score() is preceded by an exact-type check. `end` is tested with type(...) is str before the frozenset membership, and 'tracer' and 'gates_sha256' get exact-str clauses in BAD_TRACE. Prototype: list, dict, set, None and bytes ends all refuse BAD_TRACE, and check_metrics reports usable False. Exam case: end=['returned'] refuses BAD_TRACE and check_metrics REPORTED.

Release order is fixed: unregister (_MINTED, then _BY_FN) first and restore last, and only if fn.__code__ is m.code. The entry CODE_SWAPPED check fires only against a mint with a live holder (state active or exiting). Stale mints are reclaimed under the lock at every enter and exit, scanning both registries. Joining a mint re-registers it in _MINTED, which repairs a release cut short between the two pops; the sweep found that case. Prototype: the verifier's v_det reads NOT REPRODUCED (later traces PASS, registries empty). The exception sweep (384 injections per version) found no poisoned later trace on 3.11, 3.12 or 3.13.

The coverage branch of check_metrics uses 'smoke run' only when the trace is absent; otherwise it reports the real refusal text. smoke is detected as dict.get(result,'smoke') is True on a dict (subclass) result. Prototype: NOT_EXERCISED, SECTION_ABSENT and STALE_TRACE smoke results carry their real text; NO_TRACE smoke reads 'smoke run'.

Resolution has no except clause other than around the import and the PEP 562 __getattr__ call; both convert to UNRESOLVED chained with `from e`, so the async exception survives as __cause__ (L-ASYNC-EXC). Every other read (module/class/function namespaces, MRO, qualname, own __dict__ via C descriptor, staticmethod __func__) is a C getter that cannot raise synchronously, so an async exception propagates unchanged. Prototype: the exception sweep injects Timeout and KeyboardInterrupt at every line of _resolve_target, _provenance, _own_ns and _code_file_ok. The sweep re-raises any refusal not chained to the injected exception, and it completed on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, so no case swallowed the exception or turned it into another refusal.

The per-thread record is [dict id(opening)->opening, epoch] rather than a counter. Adds and pops are single C operations and idempotent, and a 'closed' flag is set last. The entry is populated before the hook is installed (the prototype found that the hook otherwise removes itself on the next event). Empty entries are dropped by close, by hop-close (the profiler is touched only on the owning thread, and only if it is ours) and by exit's detach. _THREADS and _ANCHORS are cleared whenever no tracer is active. Prototype: the sweep over every line of _open and _close shows no I4 leak on 3.11-3.13; the frozen v5e exam's leftover checks pass.

The cut code is read before resolution, so a mocked Handle._run fails before anything is touched. Each mint is registered before it is published. The whole claim-resolve-mint-activate sequence sits in `except BaseException`: _by_code is cleared, the state set to 'failed', _reclaim_locked() drops the failed holder and restores its mints, then the exception is re-raised. A retry refuses REENTRY. Prototype (verifier's script, patched only to accept the designed REENTRY): route A (audit hook refusing the second __code__ write) leaves f and g unminted and registries empty, and a later trace PASSes and restores; route B is clean; route C (real SIGALRM, BaseException) had about 35k exceptions out of __enter__ per version with 0 leaks on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13.

A PEP 562 product is accepted only if the same object is bound in the module's namespace after the call (identity scan of the values). Otherwise UNSTABLE_ATTRIBUTE refuses at entry, naming the returned function's module:qualname and file: 'declare that function where it is bound'. The product is never credited through its constant code, because that would reopen R3-B1. V10 (the module-level _lazy returned) still passes. Disclosed in over-blocking #9. Ledger row U562 (K_pep562_fresh_refused) killed.

The first act of __enter__ is an atomic claim under _LOCK: if the state is 'new' it becomes 'entering'; otherwise REENTRY is raised and recorded. Imports and __getattr__ run after the claim, outside the lock. Prototype, verifier's own_repro: A, B and D give exactly one entry, the loser gets REENTRY 'entering' recorded, score refuses REENTRY, and leftovers are clean. In scenario E, the thread that claims first wins and the main thread's `with` refuses REENTRY.

The branch is chosen from type(obj) with issubclass (C, no __class__ lookup). Class internals are read through type.__dict__['__dict__'/'__mro__'/'__qualname__'].__get__, module namespaces through ModuleType's __dict__ member, and staticmethod/classmethod through their __func__ member. Prototype: the KeyError registry, the raising lazy proxy and a metaclass whose __getattribute__ raises all resolve with 0 user side effects on 3.11-3.13. The docstring and the R1-D2 closure row become true.

This stays fail-closed: under eager_task_factory (3.12+), a child's first synchronous step runs on the parent opening's stack, so opening a section there refuses NESTED_SECTION for the whole trace. 'Sections are calls' and over-blocking #1 and #4 are rewritten to say so. Remedy: `await asyncio.sleep(0)` before cov.run_async in the child, or no eager factory; the verifier's c3 control PASSes. Version-keyed exam case (3.12+): create_task and TaskGroup refuse NESTED_SECTION, and yield-first PASSes. Prototype reproduces this on 3.12.3 and 3.13.12.

Each _Mint records gc.get_freeze_count() when it is created. At exit, if the refcount gate shows unexplained references, gc.get_referrers finds no other FunctionType, and the freeze count has changed since the mint was created, CLONE_ALIVE is recorded ('a frozen clone cannot be ruled out'). A clone of M can hide only in a freeze made after M existed. A delta is used, not 'count > 0', because the 3.12.3 build here starts with 375 frozen objects, which would over-block the exam's own V34. Prototype: all six verifier variants refuse CLONE_ALIVE on 3.11 and 3.12. Disclosed over-block: freeze or unfreeze during a trace while a traceback or frame of T is kept alive at exit. Ledger row FRZ (K_freeze_hidden_clone) killed.

FOREIGN_DEFINITION and UNSTABLE_ATTRIBUTE messages name the innermost function reached as dict.get(__globals__,'__name__'):co_qualname plus its code file, and FOREIGN_DEFINITION suggests the own-dict '.__wrapped__' path. Prototype: the verifier's repro reports names_defining_module True for both vpkg:solve and vpkg:solve2. '<string>' code in vpkg._gen is now refused by CF1 (disclosed); the closure-row sentence is made true.

Over-blocking #14 is rewritten. Code that a trace callback runs directly is never credited. Code it runs through sys.call_tracing (for example pdb's `debug` command) is credited to the section whose stack it lands on: on all versions when the callback installs a nested tracer, and on 3.12/3.13 otherwise (3.11's call_tracing does not re-arm profiling). It is added to L-RUNTIME. It is not a false PASS: the target really ran on the section's stack. A version-keyed residual case pins it. Prototype confirms: 3.11 NOT_EXERCISED, 3.12/3.13 PASS.

check_metrics' v3 usability test is `type(val) is int or (type(val) is float and isfinite(val))`, so an int is never converted. score() computes finiteness inside try/except (OverflowError, ValueError, TypeError), and an exact int compares exactly. check_metrics never raises. Prototype: 10**400 is reported and scored with no escape.

Cache wrappers are not declarable, so two wrappers can no longer map to one declared name. A 'name.__wrapped__' declaration literally names the shared body, and every run of that body is a run of what was declared. The sentence 'no two distinct callables map to one observed code object' becomes true, and L-CACHE is removed. Prototype: the verifier's own_repro refuses at entry NOT_A_FUNCTION with the remedy path.

The window is narrowed and the text made true. `if state != 'active': return False; state = 'exiting'; _by_code = {}` are __exit__'s first statements, before the lock. They contain no call or backward jump, so they are atomic under the GIL on 3.11-3.13, and the lock-wait window now reads TRACE_INCOMPLETE (prototype, own_lockwait). The remaining windows, which cannot be closed, are disclosed in L-ASYNC-EXC: an exception at __exit__'s entry (RESUME, or our hook's 'call' event for __exit__) and at __enter__'s final 'return' event through our hook. Either leaves a dead 'active' tracer: record() refuses TRACE_ACTIVE (fail closed), its equal-code mints stay for the process, and later tracers are unaffected. Prototype (entry-profiler and entry-signal): later traces PASS 3/3.

The NESTED_SECTION reason now reads 'a call there would sit on the stack of two openings of this trace'. LAZY_RESULT reads 'whatever of its body runs after the section closed does not count' and uses the normalized section. Both appear in the prototype output; no verdict depends on either text.
Two frozen violation cases expect SECTION_DECL: section '' and a confusable section with a Cyrillic е. Ledger rows D01 and D02 (DELETE_CLAUSE on each disjunct), each killed by its own case.

Every holder runs the CLONE_ALIVE check at its own exit (unchanged). Kill case K_clone_alive_inner_holder: nested tracers on f; the inner keeps a same-globals clone alive past its exit and the outer drops it. The inner must refuse CLONE_ALIVE. Ledger E09 (narrow-to-last-holder) is killed in the prototype on 3.11-3.13.

designs_all.mechanism_changes:
Numbered against v5e (styxx/protocol.py v5 region, _check_coverage, check_metrics, score). The prototype of everything below except M20 is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/1230efe6-3e44-5eb6-ad91-35910fea5db9/scratchpad/v5f/narrow/proto/impl/styxx/protocol.py (sha256 5b742054fb50...); the region alone is proto/v5f_region.py.

M1 RUNTIME. First statement of __enter__: refuse UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME (raise only) unless sys.version_info[:2] in {(3,11),(3,12),(3,13)} and getattr(sys,'_is_gil_enabled',lambda:True)() is not False.

M2 LOCK DISCIPLINE. Every locked region has exactly this shape: `try: with _LOCK: <body>; raise _Release` / `except _Release: pass`. _Release is a private BaseException subclass, raised as a fresh instance so no traceback is shared. The body never returns from inside the with. The hook and record() never take the lock.

M3 STATE MACHINE. States: new, entering, active, exiting, exited, failed, forked. _LIVE, a set of tracers in state 'active', replaces the _ACTIVE counter. record() refuses TRACE_ACTIVE for new/entering/active, TRACE_INCOMPLETE for exiting/failed/forked, and builds only on exited. _refuse_recorded appends when state != 'new'.

M4 __enter__:
(a) runtime check;
(b) under the lock: prior = state; if prior == 'new', state = 'entering'. If prior != 'new', REENTRY (raised, and recorded when entered before);
(c) `import asyncio.events; cut = Handle._run.__code__`;
(d) resolve every target outside the lock;
(e) under the lock: _reclaim_locked(); the entry CODE_SWAPPED check applies only to a registered mint with non-empty tracers and fn.__code__ is not m.code. Then mint: a new mint is registered in _MINTED and _BY_FN before `fn.__code__ = m.code`; joining an existing mint re-registers _MINTED[id(m.code)] = m. Then _STOP = cut; self._mints = joined; _LIVE.add(self); state = 'active' as the last statement before raise _Release;
(f) `except BaseException`: _by_code = {}, state = 'failed', a locked _reclaim_locked(), re-raise.
The tracer records self._pid = os.getpid() (M20).

M5 _reclaim_locked(), under the lock:
- _LIVE keeps only state 'active'.
- For each distinct mint in _MINTED.values() and _BY_FN.values(): m.tracers keeps only holders in 'active' or 'exiting'. If none remain, pop _MINTED, pop _BY_FN, then restore fn.__code__ = m.original if fn.__code__ is m.code (restore last).
- If _LIVE is empty: _THREADS.clear() and _ANCHORS.clear().

M6 __exit__:
- First statements, outside the lock: `if state != 'active': return False; state = 'exiting'; _by_code = {}`.
- Then locked:
  1. _LIVE.discard(self).
  2. Idempotent detach of each opening with closed False: pop its anchor, set frame None, pop it from its thread's dict (dropping an empty entry), set closed True, add the OPEN_AT_EXIT note.
  3. CLONE_CALLED problems.
  4. For each mint: swapped = fn.__code__ is not m.code, which records CODE_SWAPPED (every holder checks). Remove self; if no holders remain, unregister, then restore only if not swapped.
  5. _reclaim_locked().
  6. Tripwires last: for each mint, expected = 2 + (fn.__code__ is m.code). If the refcount exceeds it, gc.get_referrers looks for a FunctionType other than fn: found, CLONE_ALIVE; else if gc.get_freeze_count() != m.frozen, CLONE_ALIVE ('unprovable').
  7. If _LIVE is empty and sys.getprofile() is _hook, setprofile(None).
  8. state = 'exited', last.

M7 _Mint gains `frozen = gc.get_freeze_count()` at creation.

M8 _open:
- Normalize a str subclass with str.__str__.
- Then the checks in the v5e order: TRACE_INACTIVE, UNDECLARED_SECTION (type(section) is str and membership), NESTED walk (same tracer, cut by identity), FOREIGN_PROFILER (before any registration, outside the lock).
- Locked body, in this order:
  1. st = _THREADS.get(tid), else create [{}, 0];
  2. o = _Opening(...); self._openings.append(o);
  3. st[0][id(o)] = o;
  4. only then, if sys.getprofile() is None: st[1] = o.epoch = next(_EPOCH) and setprofile(_hook). Installing the hook before step 3 makes it remove itself on the next event; the prototype found this;
  5. _ANCHORS[id(anchor)] = o, last.

M9 _close, locked:
- If not o.closed: pop the anchor first, frame = None.
- prof = sys.getprofile(). THREAD_HOP if tid != o.tid; elif prof is not _hook, or the entry is missing, or its epoch differs: PROFILER_LOST ('may not have been observed').
- Pop o from its thread's dict. If the dict is empty, pop the entry, and setprofile(None) only if tid == o.tid and prof is _hook.
- end = end; closed = True.

M10 _hook:
- `st = _THREADS.get(get_ident()); if not _LIVE or st is None or not st[0]: if sys.getprofile() is _hook: setprofile(None); return`.
- Rest unchanged: 'call' only; _MINTED identity; globals identity leading to CLONE_CALLED for all holders; f_back walk cut at `f.f_code is _STOP`; credit exactly one opening per tracer; ambiguous; uncredited.

designs_all.exception_safety_model:
Threat: an exception (signal-handler Exception, KeyboardInterrupt, RecursionError, MemoryError) raised at any bytecode of the machinery. On CPython 3.11-3.13 with the GIL, such exceptions arrive only at eval-breaker points (RESUME at function entry, backward jumps, calls) or are raised by a profile function on the event it is handling, including OUR hook on c_call, c_return, call and return events of our own code.

E1 Lock. It can never be orphaned.
- Acquisition is atomic: RLock.__enter__ either acquires without raising, or is interrupted and does not acquire.
- Release always happens: every body ends with raise _Release, so release runs in WITH_EXCEPT_START, which is not reported to profile functions (event lists identical on 3.10.20/3.11.15/3.12.3/3.13.12).
- Any exception inside the body also takes the exceptional path.
- The hook and record() take no lock, so finalizers and signal handlers that re-enter only nest on an RLock.

E2 Credit safety. Every prefix of every mutation sequence gives no credit the spec would not give. A credit needs (a) a registered anchor executing on the chain and (b) a registered mint whose live holder's _by_code names it. The orders that guarantee this:
- _open registers the anchor last;
- _close deregisters the anchor first;
- __exit__ empties _by_code as its third statement, before the lock;
- __enter__ publishes fn.__code__ = M only after registering M;
- a failed enter clears _by_code before rolling back.
A stale anchor belongs to a returned run() frame, which is never on a live chain.

E3 Idempotent bookkeeping plus reconciliation.
- Per-thread state is a dict of openings, each opening carries a closed flag, and per-mint state is a tuple of holders, so every step is a single C operation that can be repeated.
- Any prefix left by an interruption is repaired at the next enter or exit by _reclaim_locked: it drops holders in state failed/exited/forked/entering; reclaims mints with no active or exiting holder (unregister first, restore last, only if fn.__code__ is m.code, so an interruption between the two leaves equal code, never a poisoned mint); and clears _THREADS/_ANCHORS when no tracer is active.
- Joining a mint re-registers it.
- Entry CODE_SWAPPED fires only against a live holder.

E4 State machine: record() only on 'exited', so an interrupted lifecycle leaves a state that refuses to produce a trace (TRACE_ACTIVE or TRACE_INCOMPLETE): fail closed.
- Claims are atomic: enter's claim is under the lock; exit's claim is two statements with no call or backward jump, atomic under the GIL.
- A failed enter becomes 'failed' and refuses retry.
- A forked child's tracers become 'forked'.

E5 Resolution. Nothing is touched before it completes, and the cut is read first.
- Its only except clauses (import, PEP 562) chain the exception into UNRESOLVED as __cause__.
- Every other read is a C getter that cannot raise synchronously, so an async exception propagates rather than becoming another refusal.

E6 Hook. No try and no lock. An exception in or through it propagates, and CPython drops the hook on that thread, so calls can only be under-counted (PROFILER_LOST). Self-removal never removes a chaining or foreign profiler.

E7 Residual windows, disclosed in L-ASYNC-EXC:
- (i) an exception at __exit__'s entry (RESUME, or our hook's 'call' event for __exit__), or at __enter__'s final 'return' event delivered through our hook, leaves a dead 'active' tracer: record() refuses TRACE_ACTIVE, its equal-code mints and _LIVE membership persist for the process, and later tracers are unaffected;
- (ii) an interruption inside __exit__ before the release leaves its mints held by an 'exiting' tracer (equal code, for the process) with TRACE_INCOMPLETE; a later hot swap of that function then refuses CODE_SWAPPED at entry;
- (iii) an exception between _open's registration and run's try gives OPEN_AT_EXIT and no credit;
- (iv) a second exception inside rollback or reconciliation is repaired at the next enter or exit.

Evidence:
- inject_sweep.py raises Timeout and KeyboardInterrupt, via a real SIGALRM handler, at the first execution of every executable line of _open, _close, __enter__, __exit__, run, record, _reclaim_locked, _resolve_target, _provenance, _own_ns and _code_file_ok: 384 injections fired per version on 3.11.15, 3.12.3 and 3.13.12.
- Invariants: I1 lock free (another thread acquires within 1 s); I2 no false PASS on a never-called declared target, and no overcount; I3 a fresh control trace PASSes exactly {f:1}; I4 no leak.
- Result: 0 violations of I1, I2 and I3. The 38 I4 residuals are all class (ii), in __exit__. The one remaining I4 case is __enter__'s `return self` (class (i)), reachable in reality only through our hook's return event.
- The sweep found two real bugs, which are fixed: the half-registered mint (__exit__ line 40) and the hook-install order.
- Real signals: 34.5k SIGALRM exceptions with 0 leaks of sys.exc_info across styxx calls, and 0 orphaned locks in 6 runs of 45 s. (Raising from a settrace callback leaks exc_info across trials, an artifact of the injection method; the real-signal runs show no such leak.)
designs_all.new_limits_and_overblocking:
NEW REFUSALS (over-blocking, each disclosed with its remedy):

O1 UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME: Python 3.10 and earlier, 3.14 and later, free-threaded builds. Remedy: run the harness on CPython 3.11-3.13 with the GIL.

O2 GENERATOR_TARGET: every generator, coroutine and async-generator function, including `async def` targets. Remedy: declare plain functions their bodies call. Async harnesses must factor work into sync helpers, which is a real cost for async-heavy code.

O3 NOT_A_FUNCTION for a directly declared C lru_cache/cache wrapper. Remedy, given in the message: declare 'module:name.__wrapped__' (or 'module:C.m.__wrapped__' for class-held caches). Misses count and hits do not.

O4 FOREIGN_DEFINITION for code not compiled from its defining module's file:
- dataclass-, attrs-, namedtuple- and typing-generated methods, and functions exec'd from strings even into the module namespace (co_filename '<...>');
- functions and wraps wrappers in frozen stdlib modules on 3.11+;
- sourceless (.pyc-only) modules;
- modules whose __file__ is missing or rewritten (PyInstaller-style bundles, some notebook kernels);
- any __code__ swapped in before the trace.
Remedy: declare a hand-written function in a source module (for a dataclass, __post_init__ or a method). The v5e cases V05/X47 (DA.__init__) become refusals.

O5 RESERVED_TARGET: any target in the asyncio package, and the dispatch cut under any alias.

O6 UNSTABLE_ATTRIBUTE: a PEP 562 attribute whose product is not bound in the module namespace (a fresh object per access, or a lazy re-export). Remedy: declare the function where it is bound; the message names it.

O7 cov.run in a forked child (ProcessPoolExecutor or multiprocessing with fork) raises TRACE_INACTIVE ('forked'). Child processes were never credited; now the job fails loudly instead of misreporting NESTED_SECTION.

O8 CLONE_ALIVE when gc.freeze()/unfreeze() ran after a target was minted and its minted code has references gc cannot attribute at exit (for example a stored traceback or frame of T).

O9 REENTRY for a retry after a failed __enter__, and for the losing thread of a concurrent double entry (recorded, so every declaring gate refuses).

O10 INSTANCE_PATH for a path step through an object whose __dict__ is served by a Python-level descriptor.

O11 (was undisclosed, now disclosed) Under eager_task_factory (3.12+), a child task that opens a section in its first synchronous step on a parent opening's stack refuses NESTED_SECTION for the trace. Remedy: `await asyncio.sleep(0)` first.

LIMITS CHANGED:
- L-STUB narrowed: only a stub compiled from the declared module's own file, a wraps-stamped foreign stub, or code whose co_filename was forged with code.replace is credited as the target (deliberate-only, apart from the in-module stub).
- L-RUNTIME widened: code a trace callback runs through sys.call_tracing (pdb's `debug` command) is credited where it lands, on 3.12/3.13 always and on 3.11 only through a nested settrace.
- L-ASYNC-EXC widened, with the E7 windows:
  - an exception at __exit__'s entry or at __enter__'s return through our hook leaves a dead active tracer (TRACE_ACTIVE; equal-code mints for the life of the process);
  - an interrupted exit leaves equal-code mints held (TRACE_INCOMPLETE), and a later hot swap of that function then refuses CODE_SWAPPED at entry;
  - an exception during an import or a PEP 562 __getattr__ at __enter__ becomes a chained UNRESOLVED.
- L-CODE (new): after an interrupted exit a target may keep an equal minted code object for the rest of the process.
- Cost (from the unconfirmed NOTE): the f_back walk is linear in stack depth per hit, so a recursive declared target costs O(depth^2) (about 3 s at depth 8000). The first __enter__ imports asyncio. Lock regions add one exception raise per open and close (about 1 us).
- Wording: the pure-Python profile module refuses FOREIGN_PROFILER on every version; only cProfile is 3.11-only. yappi is not detected.

LIMITS REMOVED:
- L-CACHE: a '.__wrapped__' declaration literally names the body.
- 'Counts are frame entries / generator resumptions count again': counts are calls.
- Residual R07 as a PASS residual: calling the body is exercising what was declared.

v5e EXAM OUTCOMES THAT CHANGE: V05, V07, V14, R07, X47, X54 (all verified on the prototype, identical on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13).
designs_all.risks:
What could reopen rounds 1-3:
(1) R1-B1/R2-D2 (shared code). Minting is untouched, but the provenance walk now crosses the own-dict __wrapped__ of any object. It is provenance only, never identity, so it cannot credit a sibling. Round 5 should still check that no path lets the walk's accepted link become F_T.
(2) R1-B3/R3-B2 (attribution). Unchanged except that _STOP is never cleared and asyncio cannot be minted. The risk is a future asyncio change to Handle._run; 3.14 is refused until re-validated.
(3) R1-B4 (foreign profiler). The lock discipline deliberately does NOT suspend or restore profilers, because doing so would re-create R1-B4 for C profilers. Keep it that way.
(4) R1-D1/R2-B3 (lifecycle leaks). Now rest on the state machine and _reclaim_locked, both new code. The prototype passes the frozen v5e leftover checks, the hazards (H1 0 hangs with its mutant detected, H2 20/20 with its mutant detected, H3 5/5) and the V32 stress on 3.11 and 3.13, and the closure battery holds 39/41. The two changed rows are the deliberate new refusals (dataclass __init__, generator), not reopenings.

What round 5 should attack first:
(a) The lock discipline's single CPython assumption: that WITH_EXCEPT_START's __exit__ call is never reported to profile functions. Check debug and PGO builds, other 3.11-3.13 patch releases, and profilers installed through the C API (PyEval_SetProfile) that might hook differently.
(b) CF1/CF2 bypasses a careless harness could reach: sys.modules aliasing; importlib.reload after the source moved; __file__ rewritten by tooling; the same file loaded as two modules; frozen bundles; notebooks; pytest assertion rewriting of a module that is also a target.
(c) The residual E7 windows: whether a real async exception can reach __enter__'s return or __exit__'s entry other than through our hook, and whether a dead active tracer can ever produce a scoreable trace (a harness calling __exit__ again).
(d) Reconciliation races: an 'exiting' tracer waiting for the lock while another thread's enter reclaims or joins its mint. 'exiting' holders are deliberately kept live to avoid a false CODE_SWAPPED; confirm that no ordering yields one.
(e) register_at_fork ordering: after_in_child handlers that other libraries registered earlier run before ours, with the inherited hook and a possibly held _LOCK.
(f) Over-blocking breadth: GENERATOR_TARGET for async code and CF1 for generated methods. Round 5 should measure how many committed preregs or harnesses would now refuse, and whether any refusal message fails to give a working remedy.
(g) The ledger process: completeness of the clause enumeration (an unenumerated clause is an unguarded clause); independence of the translator; any temptation to reclassify a survivor after the freeze.
(h) The UNSTABLE_ATTRIBUTE identity scan: a __getattr__ that caches in a module global and later returns a different object is fail-closed (NOT_EXERCISED), but confirm it cannot yield a false PASS.

designs_all.name: v5f "steward-and-monitor": sys.monitoring confirmed-entry credit on CPython 3.12/3.13 only, all state transitions on a signal-immune steward thread
designs_all.thesis: Replace the per-thread sys.setprofile hook with sys.monitoring local events on the minted code objects (PY_START/PY_RESUME record a pending outcome; PY_RETURN/PY_YIELD, or a PY_UNWIND past the entry offset, publish it with one dict store). Every multi-step transition (mint, restore, tool registration, sweeps) runs on one daemon "steward" thread that no Python signal handler can run on, while callers only submit (one C call) and wait. One mechanism, on 3.12 and 3.13 only, with identical outcomes; 3.9–3.11, 3.14+ and free-threaded builds refuse UNSUPPORTED_VERSION. The mint-and-anchor identity rule and the anchor/cut attribution rule of v5e are kept unchanged.

per_finding.how: Code/globals coherence. On every FunctionType link the provenance walk visits, up to and including the matching link (so it also covers the minted object and a wraps wrapper whose own __code__ was swapped), the rule is realpath+normcase(co_filename) == realpath+normcase(dict.get(__globals__,'__file__')). The check is skipped only when co_filename starts with '<' or __file__ is absent, not a str, or a .pyc. A failing link refuses FOREIGN_DEFINITION: 'its __code__ was replaced'. Prototype: both repro shapes (real.__code__=stub.__code__; FunctionType(stub.__code__, vars(mod))) refuse on 3.12/3.13. Spec text: L-STUB's premise is corrected to 'provenance proves which globals the function was built with and that its code was compiled from that module's file'. The residual narrows to in-module stubs and deliberately forged or '<...>' filenames, and the J1-X1 row is restated. New exam cases: X26b, X26c, X26d (wrapper code swapped).

Structural. There is no profile hook, and no lock is ever held on a thread that can receive a signal. Transitions run on the steward, and Python signal handlers run only on the main thread. Callers do one SimpleQueue.put and an interruptible wait. Sections open and close with single dict stores and no lock. Measured with a 60 s real-SIGALRM flood per cell. v5e: 34 hangs (3.12) and 128 hangs (3.13) plus 2.2–2.5k leaks. Prototype: 0 hangs and 0 leaks over 253k/328k iterations with 247k/325k delivered timeouts. The exam adds a fault-injection gate (another thread must always complete a trace after any single-opcode fault) and a signal-sweep gate.

The cached body is the C wrapper's real callee: the only FunctionType in gc.get_referents(wrapper), with NOT_A_FUNCTION if the count is not exactly 1. __wrapped__ is never read for a cache wrapper, for identity or for provenance; the provenance walk steps from a cache wrapper to its real callee. Prototype: restamped wrapper, only Ref.power called → NOT_EXERCISED; a miss of the declared wrapper → PASS {power:1}; identical on 3.12/3.13. Spec step 4, L-CACHE and the 'nothing is unwrapped' sentence are rewritten. Exam: X25d, V07b.

3.10/3.11 refuse UNSUPPORTED_VERSION. On 3.12/3.13 only PY_START/PY_RESUME entries can be credited, and only after confirmation. throw()/close() entries fire PY_THROW, which is never counted. Probe p1_events: on both versions, dropping, closing or throwing into an unstarted generator/coroutine fires no START/RESUME, close-at-bare-yield fires none, and a consumed two-yield generator gives START+2 RESUME. The battery pins NOT_EXERCISED for drop/close/throw on both. Exam: X74d–X74g, unkeyed.

The dispatch cut is a process-lifetime, grow-only identity map id(code)→code of every code object ever read as asyncio.events.Handle._run.__code__ (read by the caller at each enter, before anything is touched), plus the mint of it when it is minted. It is never cleared and is replaced wholesale, so callbacks read it without a lock. Membership is by identity: map.get(id(c)) is c. Prototype: X73 shape after an inner Handle._run tracer entered and exited, and while it is still active, both NOT_EXERCISED. Exam: X65b, X73b.

coverage_trace() raises [V5:UNSUPPORTED_VERSION] on any Python other than CPython 3.12/3.13 GIL builds. It is not recorded, because no trace exists. v5f installs no Python-level profile or trace function on any version, and sys.monitoring callbacks have no FastToLocals/LocalsToFast trampoline. score()/check_metrics of a /3 trace still work on every version. The 'R3 nit: f_locals cost' row is restated. Exam: X119 on 3.10/3.11 (raised; scoring still works).

The NESTED rule is unchanged. The 'Sections are calls' text and over-blocking #1/#4 are amended: under eager_task_factory, a child created on an open opening's stack runs its first step on that stack, so opening a section there refuses NESTED_SECTION for the whole trace. The remedy is 'await asyncio.sleep(0)' before opening. Prototype t_eager on 3.12/3.13: opening in the first step → NESTED_SECTION, yield first → PASS {A:f1, B:g3}. Because v5f supports only 3.12+, exam case X83 needs no version key.

Fail closed. At exit, if refcount(M_T) exceeds the explained references (mint slot, argument, installed F_T, cut map), gc finds no foreign FunctionType holder, gc.get_freeze_count()>0, and the excess is larger than the number of visible non-F_T referrers, then CLONE_ALIVE is recorded: 'cannot rule out a frozen clone'. The new over-block (a live T frame/generator/traceback held by a frozen object at exit) is disclosed. The check runs at every tracer's exit, not only the last holder's. Exam: X57b, X58b with gc.freeze(), plus the benign frozen-heap PASS V35.

FOREIGN_DEFINITION names 'declare <globals __name__>:<__qualname__> instead' for the innermost function the walk reached, keeping the file path. An incoherent link gets its own text naming the module whose function runs foreign code. Reads use dict.get on __globals__ and C slots only. The closure row is reworded. Exam: a message-content case.

Under sys.monitoring this is identical on 3.12/3.13. Probe p2 (d) and t_coexist (pdb 'debug'): code a trace or profile callback runs directly is never credited; code it runs through sys.call_tracing (pdb's debug command) is credited to the section whose stack it lands on. Over-block #14 is rewritten and the case added to L-RUNTIME. Exam pins both arms, unkeyed.

The _finite_number helper converts OverflowError into 'not a finite number' in check_metrics (usable False) and in score's guard (GateSpecError). The smoke flag is read as dict.get(result,'smoke') is True, so user __bool__ is never called. Prototype: a JSON 10**400 metric → usable False, no raise. Exam X117b covers a huge int, and a smoke value whose __bool__ raises.

A cache wrapper refuses NOT_A_FUNCTION when another _CACHE_WRAPPER with the same real callee is bound in the module dict or the holding namespace ('bind the body and declare it'). Prototype: the repro refuses. Residual: a sibling wrapper held elsewhere still shares the mint. L-CACHE is widened to 'every execution of the cached callee counts, by any route', and the line-72 sentence is qualified. Exam: X25e plus a pinned residual R12.

__exit__'s first statement submits a prebuilt exit request, so an interruption while waiting no longer matters: the steward completes the exit. There is no _ACTIVE counter that has to reach 0 (_ACTIVE is a registry, and nothing is gated on it being empty except tool release by reconcile). Residual, disclosed: an asynchronous exception at __exit__'s own first instruction (RESUME) before the put leaves the tracer active. record() then refuses TRACE_ACTIVE with the remedy 'call __exit__ again (idempotent)'. Fault injection: 5 opcode points per tracer; real-signal flood: 0 occurrences.

os.register_at_fork(after_in_child) disarms the child: it restores each mint's original code if still installed, clears local events, deregisters callbacks, frees the tool id, clears every registry, makes a fresh request queue and has no steward. The fork generation is bumped, so an inherited tracer is inert: run()/run_async() call fn with no opening, and record() refuses. Prototype on 3.12/3.13: a fork ProcessPoolExecutor made inside a section returns job values with the child's tool freed, and the parent shows SECTION_ABSENT with clean state. The 'bootstrap frame' sentence and R2-B3 row are limited to threads.

New over-block entry: a generator/coroutine/async-generator object of T created before the trace, or in an earlier trace, runs T's original code and is never credited; crediting original code would reopen R1-B1/X48. When a missing target has CO_GENERATOR/CO_COROUTINE/CO_ASYNC_GENERATOR, the NOT_EXERCISED message adds that hint (static). L-WHERE's example is narrowed to objects created during the trace.

The result test is issubclass(type(result), dict) plus dict.get or dict.keys, so no subclass method runs. NO_TRACE is split into 'no coverage_trace key' and '<type>, not an exact dict'. check_metrics 'present' uses the same test. Prototype: a defaultdict result → PASS. Exam: X93c.

Structural. v5f never calls sys.setprofile, threading.setprofile or settrace, so there is no self-removal. FOREIGN_PROFILER, PROFILER_LOST and THREAD_HOP retire. Prototype p2 (e1–e3) and t_coexist: cProfile, a Python setprofile, a Python settrace, and coverage.py (ctrace and sysmon cores) all run alongside with exact counts. Exam: a chaining profiler started in a section is still installed after close and exit and sees its later events.

The provenance walk steps through the own-dict __wrapped__ of any link, still bounded (object + 16 hops) and cycle-detected. The instance dict is read only through the C getset/member descriptor that stores it, found via type.__dict__['__mro__'] and type.__dict__['__dict__'], so metaclass and user __getattribute__ are bypassed. A user-defined __dict__ descriptor stops the walk and is never called. It opens no false PASS beyond L-STUB: the minted object is still the one bound at the name, and every FunctionType link must be coherent. Exam: V11c ('@logged @memoize def fit' → PASS), X30d ('__dict__' property on a link is never called).

_open normalizes a section whose type is a str subclass (issubclass(type(s), str)) to its exact value with str.__str__. Any other non-str refuses UNDECLARED_SECTION. Prototype: a (str, Enum) section → PASS. Exam: StrEnum and numpy.str_-style cases.

Rule for _check_trace_shape: every exact-type test precedes any hash or comparison of the value it guards (end, and the keys of the trace, openings and uncredited). Prototype: end=['returned'] → [V5:BAD_TRACE]. Exam: X103b–d (list end, dict end, str-subclass end).

Entry CODE_SWAPPED fires only against a mint with live holders. Every steward transition starts with an idempotent _reconcile that releases mints with no active holders (restoring only if still installed) and drops orphan anchors and pendings. Fault injection on 3.12: 0 POISON in 10,241 caller-thread and 5,027 steward-thread single-opcode faults.

Resolution has no except clause other than the two conversions the spec mandates (import, and a module's PEP 562 __getattr__), both chained.
